I apolagise for the title, but I want to focus more on Doom³ for this review, since that's the strongest aspect of  Doom 3: BFG Edition.
Doom 3 is a welcome revamp of the classic Doom titles in my eyes.
There, I said it.
I know there's lots of outcry and controversy surrounding Doom 3 and 2016, mainly because the fans believe them to "not be Doom games" and they're "too generic and Call of Duty-ish". I can understand these criticisms. Really, I can.
There is a bit too much of a focus on the story in 3, and as a result, feels less like a Doom game, as it takes the focus off just killing monsters and progressing each level.
Now this would hurt more if the story sucked. It doesn't.
I wasn't engaged as much as say, Half Life 2 or F.E.A.R 2, but I was interested in where it was going. The story is pretty generic and unspecial by today's standards, and it does drag it down a bit because of this.
But really, aside from not caring about the music in this game (when compared to the last two and their expansions), this game is just pure enjoyment from beginning to...well, maybe not the VERY end.
I couldn't help thinking how much of a great successor it is to the originals. It feels like a total overhaul, of course, but an upgrade more than anything. The horror aspect (no not the jumpscares, I mean the atmosphere) really adds to it, creating much more tension and suspense, which the originals had none of, and of which I strongly believe works well with the Doom formula.
Honestly: it's just nice to experience a game where paying attention to the story doesn't change much for the overall fun.
the level design is pretty engenious, employing new techniques of furthering the action, teleporters that you have to find a way to use, operating cargo lifts that you can control yourself, and many more add to the growing list of new gimmicks which outlines how different this game is to the last two.
Unfortunately the ending really stops this game from being great:
So yeah, a pretty rushed ending, which is a real shame because of the massive amount of build up.
Even the graphics are still very good (on everything but the humans, the humans look very dated) considering the time it was released. It even performs well. I think the lowest FPS I can remember dipping to was 53. I can appreciate a game that can run well even when I'm charging my laptop, and this one delivers on that front really well.
Overall, I REALLY like this game. I think it is pretty underrated; not F.E.A.R 2 underrated maybe, but still majorly overlooked.
If I were to give an arbitrary score out of ten I'd give it a solid 7.

Summary: If you are an RTS fan, this game is worth your time. It is not overly complex, has clean graphics, cool upgrades, and the unit animations are cool. Now there are a lot more factions too, which each have their own perks/benefits.
Pros
+You must carefully balance your economy, expansion and amenities to balance happiness/pop growth, while managing food, wood, stone and iron resources (for stronger enemies, to upgrade buildings (which are required for happiness etc).
+you have to fight off enemy NPC's and enemy players AI or human if you choose, all the while trying not to starve or run out of wood throughout the winter.
+food is an interesting mechanic as you have to save food to be able to purchase a sector (after you clear any enemies on it). So you can't just expand willy nilly.
+weather mechanic that makes sense (you use more food/wood in winter) but it doesn't last too long so it's not super annoying. Buying up new land using your food reserves just before winter though..that can cause you some problems..so ya, keep an eye on that.
+each faction has a unique unit, and some units/research upgrades and usually they each have a specific perk.
+never had a game crash despite EA (which is pretty cool). Did have units get stuck here and there, but you can move them and fix it yourself.
+game takes a match or two to learn, but after that you should be ok. forces you to find that balance between expansion/army size and defense but doesn't go off the deep end with regards to difficulty.
+devs are always tweaking the game, adding new buildings/stuff and actually listen to player base (which is frigging rare in an EA game nowadays).
CONS
-Just one enemy unit got behind my lines and "captured" an area full of my buildings...all buildings then started to burn, and couldn't be repaired unless i "captured" the point back again. I get the guy attacking my buildings...but capturing the area with my buildings in it and having them burn...thats pretty damn stupid (you can mitigate this by having a defense tower, but they cost upkeep and can cause you gold shortage early on if you expand too quickly).
-can be hard when playing with multiple AI bc they all seem to attack you for some reason (that sucks bc you can't fight all of them and win..or if you can, post it online so i can see how lol).
subjective points:
game is slower paced than some RTS (this may be a pos or neg as some may like this *personally i like it...not everything has to be like starcraft with 30 clicks a minute).
graphics are not AAA top of the line, but art style is unique and unit animation is pretty cool (to me i like it and find it enjoyable to watch the units working and moving around as it looks cool)...watch a few vids to see if the art style is to your liking.
some of the special win conditions are harder than others (i.e. ygraddisil requires like 2000 food or something, whereas the sword of odin requires you to capture several mines, capture the volcano, build a special smith and then make 3 parts of the sword)..way more involved/harder to do sword of odin. Again though...this may not be a negative to some as it is just a different way to win the game (you don't have to do it either, as you could just get another victory type).
Final Thoughts:
Overall, i recommend this game...its very playable as is and thus far i have really enjoyed it, even after nearly 50 hours. The factions are similar but different enough to justify switching them up, and ultimately it strikes a great balance between challenging and fun. *also a good way to introduce your younger kids to RTS (lol my 7 year old daughter likes watching me play this game).

This game is a good example of how you don’t have to sacrifice gameplay for a good story. Trying not to spoil it you play as "the kid" and you attempt to restore the bastion. It is of course much more than that though and the story is very well done with a great ending. The gameplay its self is amazing for this type of game, combat is fairly simple and yet it allows the user to change how he fights and defends. The best feature of this game is neither the gameplay or the story but rather the soundtrack and the narrator. In a lot of gams a narrator can be a pesky annoyance but this narrator helps tell the story as you do the levels, this way of telling the story gives a new way to explain events the kids past life and what things are without forced monologue to help us understand the world.
Combat in the game is also very simple but yet incredibly fun and challenging. You will get a number of weapons on the game and depending on how you like to fight I’d say there is a perfect combination for you. The game also has a col loot system that feels natural and will help you upgrade your weapons.
The graphics are simply stunning, it looks like the whole game was painted and just came to life, and the soundtrack just fits in perfectly. This isn’t a big budget came the story is massively complex but it was a truly fun game to play, admittedly taking 7 hours to play through but there was so much i didn’t do and i still feel the urge to play again and make different choices. The flaws of this game are nonexistence, now that’s not to say this is the best game ever  but it is a game that does what it does very well and i would say this is a very well done game.

and for all you taco lovers, here is a nifty taco recipe!
Ingredients
KC's Nifty Taco Recipe
Ingredients
1 lb. lean ground beef
1 medium onion, chopped
1 teaspoon chili powder
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
1 (8-oz.) can tomato sauce
12 taco shells
6 oz. (1 1/2 cups) shredded American or Cheddar cheese
2 cups shredded lettuce
2 tomatoes, chopped
3/4 cup salsa
3/4 cup sour cream, if desired
Steps
1) Heat oven to 250°F. In medium skillet, brown ground beef and onion over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes or until beef is thoroughly cooked, stirring frequently. Drain.
2) Stir in chili powder, salt, garlic powder and tomato sauce. Reduce heat to low; cover and simmer 10 minutes.
3) Meanwhile, place taco shells on ungreased cookie sheet. Heat at 250°F. for 5 minutes.
4) To assemble tacos, layer beef mixture, cheese, lettuce and tomatoes in each taco shell. Serve with salsa; top with sour cream.

Mostly negative reviews on this, decided to buy in on sale any ways... I think it's a potentially good game with a lot of room for improvements. The graphics are okay, the controls take a little getting used to but nothing horrible.
Pros:
+ Decent graphics
+ Plain old tower defense without unnecessary bells and whistles
+ Lots of levels
+ Lots of towers to unlock
Cons:
- No keyboard shortcuts for building, upgrading; none that I was aware of any way
- Poor sound; the music is repetitive and some sound effect are terribly annoying, e.g. dying goblins
- Not a lot of explanation about the interface, level system, abilities, etc.
- Not very well balanced; too easy to get loads of money
- Towers are not very intelligent; they will sometimes ignore a flying boss if a walking boss is also in range but behind
All in all, I think the game is not worth the full price (yet), however if you like tower defense games you will definitely enjoy it. The developers should focus on playability, clarity and strategic abilities. The latter mainly because the building spots are limited and the creeps will follow the least dangerous path and not just the shortest, which can be very frustrating because of its unpredictability. It's a nice twist, but the maps are sometimes not very suited for it.
E.t.a.: I bought the game for € 3,74 in a sale which is a reasonable price for this game. The full price is not worth it and I wouldn't recommend it at that level.
Also, I deleted comments that attacked me in person. You can talk trash about my review or the game, I don't care, but stating that I am a person with low standards because I recommend this is unfair and has nothing to do with the game or the review.

First is a guide for how to unlock DLC characters without spending real money and utilizing every character in the game. For my review please scroll ahead.
HOW TO UNLOCK ALL CHARACTERS WITHOUT REAL MONEY:
Step 1: Pick a character and start by viewing their demontrations. It teaches you the basics for that character.
Step 2: Do that characters trials. Some require practice and patience but none are terribly difficult. Watch the demo's and pay attention to timing.
Step 3: Go to traning mode and practice what you have learned. (Does not reward Fight Money, but helps with completing next steps.)
Step 4: Do that characters story mode. They're one round fights with full meters against brain dead AI.
Step 5: Do survival mode with that character and complete Easy and Normal modes. Hard and Hell are there too, but require a mastery of the game to complete. This is where the game starts to get challening, so learning your character through trials and training is essential.
Step 6: Pick a new character and repeat.
*Completing the story campaign will also net you fight money and it can be done twice with the extra mode that unlocks after your first playthrough.
**You can also earn fight money by completing the daily and weekly missions and leveling up your characters in online matches.
Once you have done this with all the characters you should have enough fight money to unlock all DLC characters without having to spend real money. In the process you will familiarize yourself with every character and become much better at the game.  (Don't listen to those who say this  game is light on single player content. There is plenty to do.)
With this process I have bought all DLC characters, including the latest Ed, two alternate costumes and one stage, and still have enough Fight Money left over to unlock the next character as soon as they're released. So if you feel like Capcom is forcing you to buy stuff, you're playing it wrong.
REVIEW:
Pros:
Great fighting system. Diversify your strategy by mixing up cross-overs, overhead attacks, dash up throws, hit confirms and reversals to always keep your opponents guessing. Combos are performed with precise timing, button mashers are not rewarded in Street Fighter.
Great soundtrack. Retro character tracks have been remade with full intrumentals and give a great sense of nostalgia. They are recognizable but fresh. Brand new tracks are well composed too and add to the drama of the fighting.
Lots of single player content that is both challening and rewarding. See the above process.
Online experience is always subjective, but when I filter connection settings to 4-5 bars, most of the matches are lag free and don't take long to get into even during off peak hours.
Cons:
Little content for the base game. If you just bought the game and are eager to go head to head with your friends, the lack of characters and stages at first is dissapointing. To unlock content it will cost you money or you will have to take the time to complete the single player content.
Steep learning curve. The lack of an arcade mode does not cater to beginners or causals who like to practice against various AI bots in a difficulty of their choosing. There is the survival mode, but losing a single round means starting all over, a punishment that most people would consider too severe.
Story mode is lacking. Character stories are very short and simple to complete. The cutscenes for the most part don't add much of a story at all. The added story mode does have some nicely done in engine cutscenes and the dialouge is passable, but most of it doesnt make sense and only serves as a segway into the next fight.
Conclusion:
Considering that all DLC characters will be free to the dedicated players who earn Fight Money, I dont mind there being little content at first. It's a better deal than having more immediate content but then hitting a paywall for future characters.If you take the time to complete the single player content and practice with all the characters then you will be rewarded with enough Fight Money to unlock a substantial amount of content such as new characters, stages, costumes and colors. How you spend it is up to you. The game is challenging but the demo's and trials are there to help. The more you play, the better you get, the more you can unlock and the bigger the game becomes.
If you're looking for a fighting game with 40+ characters unlocked from the start and an easy arcade mode you can button mash your way through, then Street Fighter V is not for you.

Ok, best mention the power armor in the flowerbed first - I don't like Bethseda's recent 'Content Club' addition with pay to play mods, I don't think it's a good direction to go in. I don't intend to give them any money for it.
Now I've said that, on with the review.
I love Fallout 4. I haven't played any of the previous Fallout games so can't compare it to them, but I have spent lifetimes in Morrowind, Oblivion, and so on.
Fallout 4 hits a sweet spot for me, it's a big open world first person shooter with a decent storyline, tons to explore and do, and a few choices thrown in along the way.
Plot-wise, your choices don't really affect much. There are several factions you can align with but the endgame doesn't really change. But you get to make the important choices like 'Do I run up and hit this super mutant with a sharp stick, or stand half a mile away and drop a nuke on him', 'Shall i stomp around the city in mighty power armor dispensing high velocity justice, or get up close wearing only pants and sunglasses using the pointy end of a crowbar.'
In a way that's quite liberating, you're unlikely to break the storyline and fail quests, so just play how you want to and have fun. And there's a lot of fun to be had.
Alongside the explore, fight and run away gameplay, there's a whole settlement building activity, something I've not encountered in a shooter before. I found this, more than anything else really sucked me into the world. As you progress, you can start building places for some of the wasteland survivors to call home. As they grow and become functioning settlements, it felt like I was really making a difference in the Commonwealth. I actually started caring about the settlers. Well, most of them. Some are idiots.
Overall, would I recommend Fallout 4? Yes, whole heartedly. I feel like I've lived in the Commonwealth, had a blast wandering around with some of the in-game travelling companions, brought hope to survivors, killed a lot of bad guys, seen some cool sights and had a great deal of fun.
Regardless of how you feel about Bethseda's paid mods, Fallout 4 is worth a go. I don't have any of the DLC addons yet, but will grab them in a sale, and fully expect to play through the game a few more times.
There are a couple of websites where skilled and dedicated fans have created some amazing mods which generally work well, and are all free. These have definitely enhanced the gameplay and are worth a look.
So grab Fallout 4 in a sale, skip the paid mod nonsense, and I think you'll get your moneys worth .. I did.

I am going to be extremely critical because I want this game to be good. I will also use The Legend of Zelda as a good reference point in several aspects because that is what the game wants to be like.
It is a gorgeous game with great exploration and ideas that are ruined by flaws in combat, effectively no way of interacting with your environment or obtaining new items to allow you to complete puzzles or interact with your environment and exploring the world with too much walking especially in the desert area of the game.
I have seen lots of reviews saying that this is like a 3D like Zelda game with exploration and good combat. Honestly, yea i can see it and I enjoy the art style and the overall feel of the game. It just isn't polished or really fun and loses its charm after the first dungeon. The dungeons honestly are the most fun part about it.
The combat gets repetetive and although you feel the impact of your swings it all turns into circle the enemy and charge your attacks, swing, and repeat until it's dead. The first boss was challenging although somewhat too difficult until I found out you can just pause the game, eat food or chug potions, and run around while your health regens. The food isn't difficult to make because with enough time you can just run around the main character's home and makes stacks of infinite food. Then one boss was literally wait around until its weak point comes out, but he doesn't let his actual attackable spot out of his body until a repetetive cycle of move a quarter around a circle and shoot a ball of arcane magic literally about 7 times in a row and it takes forever. It took nearly 4 to 5 cycles of this just to defeat this boss. It was by far the most boring fight and easiest because you literally just stop and when he shoots the ball, you move to the side.
I am going to give the game and the devs huge props on making a gorgeous world that you want to explore. I am however, going to complain that it takes forever to walk to places and this is most noticeable in the desert. Literally dunes of sand and lots of walking back and forth which is just unecessary or can be resolved by adding a horse or faster method of travel. You have a sprint, but you sprint, stop to let it charge back up, sprint more, and repeat. When your stamina runs out you walk slower than you originally were walking. Traveling in this gorgeous world is painful and takes so long. Then, after completing your objective you have to walk slowly through the same area to get back or sometimes you compelte the objective, walk back to get your next objective and are told to walk through the exact same place you just were at. Another idea to fix this issue is maybe let the player teleport to totems or waypoints from the map after discovering and saving at one. This would eliminate walking through the area you just got done walking through for the 3rd time.
Crafting is cool. Until you make iron stuff then everything else is useless until gold which again makes everything else useless. There are only 3 types of magic and they all do the same thing except do a different type of damage and there is literally just a weak and strong version which do the same thing and look the same except maybe adds a new visual effect. 4th magic spell that acts like a grapple hook, but you only use it in the final dungeon and is only useable on these weird blue squares instead of being able to use it anywhere like the grapple hook. So pretty useless
Also, in the Legend of Zelda you had items that let you interact with your environment or even use them in combat. You don't get that in this game. You don't have a boomerang, you can't use ice magic to freeze water and make platforms. You can't get a sand wand that builds up blocks of sand to climb to higher platforms. You get your same basic fighting with simple magic that is effectively another method of killing your enemy instead of circling around them with your sword you will shoot magic, run back some few feet and shoot magic and rinse and repeat.

I received this game from the developer during its very first version, and I've been continuously playing ever since.
In short, do I recommend this game? Yes! However, if you are not a fan of Zelda-esque games, then I would probably look into it a bit more.
Here are some pros:
- Fun Story
- Female Protagonist (I always find a female protagonist fun :P )
- Smooth gameplay and game mechanics
- Crafting system is easy to use/understand, and that makes it fun to do
- Cooking is fun and easy
- Foraging makes you want to constantly explore
- Great soundtrack
- Characters and enemies are creative and always interesting to come into contact with
- Game design is very well done. I really enjoy the way the world/map is designed
- Graphics may seem crude to some people, but personally I really enjoy them. I love the colorful world and characters. There's also something nostalgic about the graphics as well, almost like I'm playing on my N64 again :D
I was going to write a list of cons here, but honestly I really can't think of any cons that haven't already been fixed or patched. Plus, given the fact this is an early access game I find it unfair to point out "can't access part of map" or "this aspect is a bit buggy".
We've all played early access games where we have PAID MONEY and received absolute broken crap.
This on the other hand is a well made and designed game that is constantly progressing and being fixed/patched.
All-in-all, I honestly do recommend this game. If you love Zelda, you'll absolutely LOVE this. If you love exploration games, you'll want to get this. If you like games where there is an intensive crafting system and giant skill trees, then... well... you *might* like this.
Windscape is charming to its core, and I absolutely adore it. Get it while it's hot, and support indie devs ;)

2) The battle lounge still does not show the ping of the host.
3) Queuing for an online match takes 10-15 minutes for me, since nobody plays anymore lol.
4) CapCom doesn't communicate with its customers.
So all in all, if you want to try out a fighting game and you know StreetFighter, because it is the most mainstream one, don't. Try Guilty Gear, Tekken or KOF instead. They suck much less.

Wow, where to start?
I've been playing this game since December of 2013, and I have to tell you, it was unforgiving back then, with a steeeeeep difficulty in the early game. This game has come a long way, and I'm so glad I pre-purchased 6 months before early-access release.
It's been like watching a child grow up, first helpless, then crawling, fumbling around to walk, then from a walk to a run.
But enough with the metaphors, and my history with the game, let's get on to some of my favorite features of the game!
(and there is a lot of it)
This game is rich with content, from the vastness of space to the variety of flora and fauna, you can definitely get lost each time you visit its' universe. Each of the seemingly endless planets has their own plants, animals, and lively colonies. They all have their own dangers, including pits of acid, falling debris from space, dangerous nocturnal creatures. This all really changes how you approach survival for every location you visit!
(There is such a variety of weaponry here, it's hard to know where to start!)
Like to kill from a distance? check. Want to kill by slicing something to death? check. Blow everything up? check. Bows, swords, guns-guns-guns, rockets, etc., will help you
survive. If you want to jump high, dart quickly or bounce around, well there is tech to help you do that.
While multiplayer in games like Terraria can be hectic, if there are too many players, Starbound welcomes them with open arms. I've been on some public servers where I never found anyone to bother me (which can be good for building a secluded colony). But, this doesn't have to be that way, you can party up with your friends (sometimes acquaintances), and search the universe together.
With Starbounds bookmarking feature, you and your friends can keep up with the planets you have found, and build a civilization together.
One note about the Server system, it's not hard to use or maintain. I've never had issues with running a server stably on a Mac or Windows system and have played between both on many servers. Updates are easy through Steam, and your clients can play without issues.
This game can be difficult at times, but this is a good thing. The game is meant to have you think and be challenged it every step of your adventure.
From the aforementioned acid pools to deeps of lava, to monsters that will rip your face off, there is always something that is going to make you think about how you are going to survive. I've been very happy with the progression of the game, and how hard it can be to live, without the correct gear, or approach. You won't be without something to keep you on your toes, and so far in my time with Starbound, I'm not finding many situations where it is too easy or dull.
While the early days of early access have been a grinding and difficult task (while still fun), this game has rounded out to be something special. I've been on a planet making camp for the night, sleeping away and in awe, as the night sky was lit up by a meteor shower. There were times of frustration when fighting a boss, and losing over and over, but then the satisfaction of ridding the universe of an evil was both a relief and a reward.
It's had its' ups and downs, criticism and praise. And overall, it has lived up to all the promises that were made, in my opinion (they even came through with a DRM-free version for previous backers). I really can't wait to see where Chucklefish takes us in the upcoming weeks, months and years with this game. I keep coming back for more and am satisfied each and every time.
I'll recommend this to anyone who has played Minecraft, Terraria or something similar, you WILL NOT be disappointed.

Drawing on a variety of beloved children's stories like "Alice In Wonderland" and "The Neverending Story", "Fran Bow" is what would happen if "Pan's Labyrinth' was transformed into an adventure game.
Much like it's action-adventure equivalent "Alice: Madness Returns", the game's appeal comes largely from it's ability to mix beauty with grostequery in such a fashion that even the more horrific segments of the game feel oddly natural. One would think that images of conjoined twins and seven-foot skeletons would be a deterent, though strangely not in this game. This ease is then helped by the game's protagonist, who looks like what would happen to Angela Anaconda if you took away her sass, and is aided further by the retro-style grapics reminiscent of Terry Gilliam animation from the late 1960s. Indeed, the characterisation of Fran is very well realised, especially with regard to the character's innocent nature.
The only real complaint about Fran Bow is that it isn't as long as some of the other point and click adventures out there. The ending also feels stunted because as a player the ending revelation is overly sign posted. However, there are plenty of elements that redeem these flaws. Games like "Day of The Tentacle" and "Grim Fandango" may offer more playing hours for about the same price, though perhaps not so much variety. They certainly don't treat players to quite so many mini-games, each one turning "Fran Bow" into a tribute to the classics.
All in all, "Fran Bow" is an interesting game that is more than worthy of multiple play throughs, especially if you want to fully immerse yourself in the plot (and get all the achievements).

Which is why I'm mad at the ending. The game leaves way too much unresolved for my taste. I'm fine with a thought provoking and cryptic ending that leaves you guessing (like an allegory or something... Braid?), but this ending seemed more like the writers got lazy and didn't want to do the work of creating any kind of closure. Even if you were to build a good theory regarding what was going on (and the internet is abuzz with this topic if you look it up), there is no good explanation as to why everything happened as it did. There was just too much introduced over the course of the story for the ending as it stands to leave anything but dissatisfaction for me.
The story I'm creating about the ending is that they were going to write another chapter, and then for some reason production got rushed. That's the most satisfying explanation of the ending for me.

I have mixed feelings about this game. It has many good ideas, but some of them are poorly executed.
I love a crafting system that was added to the game. Building your settlements, upgrading power armour or weapons can be really fun.
Graphic wise this game is beautiful. Although engine is slightly dated, addition of GodRays and Volumetric Fog creates a really nice atmosphere.
Every location has an artistic touch making you feel that you truly explore post-apocalyptic wastelands. So what's wrong for with this game you ask?
For starters main story in kinda meh. The whole Institute and Sync plot in for the most part uninteresting. To be honest I'm 138 hours in the game and I mostly do side quests,
since they are more interesting. During this playtime I encountered many annoying bugs that are not fixed even 2 years after game release. I'm talking about glitchy NPC path finding, that can break some quests or make using of companions simply very annoying (they get stuck all the time). There were also few CTDs without any error log or crash dump, so save a lot. Built in autosave feature is not very good, so I wouldn't rely on it.
Second main flaw is the speak system it doesn't add much to your or NPC actions. Downside of it is that you don't have much control which settlement will join you and which not. Of course you could opt out from doing a quest, but that will lock subsequent quests. For example if you get a quest to help defeat riders in some settlement in most cases it will automatically join you. You don't have an option to chose whether you want them to join or not. Persuade skill in dialogues with NPC is used mostly to raise caps amount for the quest and nothing more for majority of the game.
Combat system is... How to put this? I would say it's hilarious. VATS is useless for the most part, fighting like in every other FPS is much more effective. Combat system in general is very unbalanced. At the beginning of the game, when you leave the Vault 111 you will be teared to pieces by any enemy you'll encounter. Raiders will nade spam you. Then in first hour of gameplay you find a Power Armour that you can use, and from now on there is rarely any challenge in combat. If you find a challenging enemy you just upgrade your Power Armour or find a better model like Mark II or something, or just use a Jet (Slow motion) to increase your DPS. This continues through out the rest of the game. Enemy AI is also not very smart and tends to rush at you. Beware on kamikaze Mutants though. They carry a Mini Nuke, which might be dangerous at the beginning of the game.
Bottom like it is rather a good game, but die hard Fallout fans may find themselves disappointed.
Also there is Creative Club (paid mods) controversy going on right now. Be aware that this change introduced a need to log in to Bethesda servers even when you want to use free mods. The problem is that Creation Club or Mods don't work for many non US living players at the moment. There is some problem with servers rejecting players from non US region and it causes game to crash when you click Creation Club or Mods in main menu. But if you plan to play without mods you're good to go.

A classic game, easily my favourite Doom game so far. Graphically advanced enough to be creepy, yet old school enough to remain true to Doom's overall feel of Horror survival.
The campaign is Solid, with challenging encounters throughout the game, a decent enough mix of tasks to remain novel and a diverse enough set of environments to keep from getting boring.
Unlike past and following Dooms, this game does use reloading, which can slow the pace of the game but creates more tension during firefights. I'm on the fence about whether this is better for the franchise, but it works in this particular instalment.
Note, this game is decently old now so don't get it if you're looking for a detailed and graphically dynamic visual experience. It's smooth, thematically consistent, and doesn't take away from the action, which is more than enough for a game of this age.
Check this game out if you enjoyed previous Dooms, or the latest Doom and want some mid range retro action. It's quite good!

It's quite "simple". You are a thing. You run. You jump. You dodge. The interesting bit is that you can change your color from blue to red and vice versa, which is really neat and has been done in the past and only recently with Outlander as well.
This game is for hardcore players. Seriously. I consider myself an above average skilled gamer, esp. with platformers, but this game got me on the mini boss fight in level THREE on EASY (there are 2 more difficulties). It gets frantic pretty quick, the levels are really long and save points are more or less fairly placed on the maps. You are constantly being chased by a purple beam of death, which adds to the frantic nature of the game. Double jumping, wall jumping, switching colors multiple times within 2 seconds while jumping and dodging spikes...yea...nope. Just cannot cope with that.
Usually I wouldn't blame a game on my deficiencies, BUT the game's controls are horribly floaty. There is no precision here, but it is absolutely required.
Conclusion: If you want a really challenging game with an interesting mechanic, are not prone to suffering epileptical attacks and can cope with the dodgy controls, go for it when it's on sale. Otherwise: Good effort, but only a b product in my opinion.

Doom 3 with a little BFG sprinkled on top.. Where to begin.
Includes Ultimate Doom & Doom II: Hell on Earth WITH controller support. No, they aren't the Brutal Doom versions we've all come to love, they are the original can't look up and down because doing so would destroy the universe (and early 90s young Carmack/Romero game engines). These two games coming with achievements alone was enough of a reason for me to buy at the sale price, I enjoyed every last second ripping my way through the games on ultra violence.
Yes, they censored the secret levels and replaced the enemies with stock former humans. No big deal, who doesn't have wolf 3d, doom collections, and brutal doom by now anyway?
As for Doom III (the changes), they gave us a somewhat "remastered" version with out of the box wide screen HD support and a few other goodies, like the ability to see (ಠ‿ಠ).. Honestly, I bought Doom 3 at release and I just turned my brightness up and would get frustrated to hell when an imp would spawn in my face (and the obligatory imp behind your back that ALWAYS comes with them). So I welcome the shoulder mounted flashlight, but I do miss cracking skulls with the flashlight as a weapon with more damage than the fists. Minor trade. As for complaints about the game being too bright, I think the new versions offers a very nice contrast as areas with power and lights are quite well lit, dark areas are so dark you cant see without the flash light. Keep flash light off if you want to get scared to death. I do agree that the FOV is very odd, I set mine to 95 and once I grew used to that everything seemed fine. All in all this is a solid re-release.
Doom III as a game is quirky, and lacks many of the elements that made the Doom games ...Doom.. and brought us more down the path of a Doom-Esque survival horror. I sorely miss the awesome Sound Blaster Pro 2 era awesome music blasting. There are many moments in this game that will make you jump at night with your headphones cranked, and many predictable moments to offset that. You'll quickly learn to always check behind you as soon as you kill that imp that just spawned, and you'll learn to be ready to spray down a mob the moment you pick up that armor.  At times it seems dull and uninspired, other times it becomes very thrilling and high energy, sometimes you'll feel your brain aching when you try to listen to that new PDF audio which immediately gets drowned out by some other talking and loud noises simultaneously. You'll cry when you realize how often you manage to have full armor but only a few health points left with no healing kits in sight. Save and save often! Either way it's just one of those games you just feel the need to keep on playing and the 10~ hours are very rewarding, especially when you come back again on a harder mode.
Doom 3 is a solid 8/10 game with graphics FAR beyond par for the year of release.
Doom 3 BFG with its enhancements with Ultimate Doom & Doom 2 on sale for 6.50 is a 10/10.

Northgard is an hybrid RTS/Settlers game, it's awesome, and it's still on Early Acess. A quick glance at it, and it might look really simple, but randomly generated starting tiles, a lot of different clans with unique units and playstyles, hazards such as blizzards, rat infestations, earthquakes and invasion, a load of possible ways to achieve victory, and so forth, always keeps the game fresh and fun to play. The best parts is that the devs are really investing their time in this, and actively hear to the feedback and participate in the communities (steam discussions/reddit/discord), and the result is one of the best RTSs I've played in years.
The current main problem with this game is that: it still doens't have servers, and no punishment for quitting a match, so it's pretty common to take 10-20 minutes trying to find a game, or creating one, and all of a sudden see all the players quitting because it's either lagged because of the host, or because they spawned in a bad spot. I know the game is in Early Acess, and that the dev team said they would arrange this by the official release of the game, but take this into consideration if you're looking for the multiplayer experience in this game.
Gameplay wise, my only concern is the lack of hotkeys for structures, queued actions for villagers and others small details that makes you go back and forth on the screen, and it gets tiresome after a couple matches.

[First Impression]
Wow! Amazing! I found this game during the steam summer sale & stuck watching the trailer because of how atmospheric it was. The artwork of this game is truely beautiful.
Why did I buy the game though? Well, because it looked a lot like a mix of my favorite childhood games (e.g. The Settlers II, Stronghold Ledgends, Warcraft III).
So after a few hours of trying to master the quests of this game in singleplayer vs 2 bots, I got to admit that I am in love with this game! But I'd like to mention a few things:
This caught me offguard,
I remember playing the Settlers or Stronghold for hours, while after 5 minutes of playing Northguard the "enemy" bots (On easy difficulty!) started to achieve their first "victory points"..
Some things I realized while playing:
I do realize that there is a limitation for a reason & one can upgrade lots, but for me - planning and structuring cities is fun, and I'd like to be free in doing so. Maybe add more upgrades to bigger areas or the "home lot"?
I started off in a map, where I wasn't able to get stone until the late endgame really, which bothered me, because I wasn't able to upgrade anything unless I bought ressources - which is expensive because Kröwns are only to be obtained by building markets or trading posts (which I found out about waaay to late)
Other than that: Why are farms limited to certain lots? I realize that there are hunters, fishers & sheep farms, but I'd like to be able to build farmland in more places (since food is a gamechanger in this game)
I spent "hours" waiting for my chance to buy more land & when my time came, winter came..
I had such an overload of wood & so much food during summers - yet, I had no Kröwns or stone.. The markets or ports would be ideal in my opinion. Options to sell certain ressources for a set price of other ressources for example.
And: More trading partners! Like after building a port, maybe give the option to trade with foreign powers (or "at home", for the sake of the story)
Soo: Different kind of mines would be awesome. And while at it: They expire way to quickly. Maybe make them work faster while supplies (food/wood/happiness) are great, but let them work slower in winters or while supplies are bad, so that overall they are able obtain more ressources in a longer period of time
Why not let the ones working in or around the place repair it? I feel like it takes way too long for me to make the guys working in the burning house run back to the city hall to become a citizen again, just to repair it.. (with bigger terretorries especially)
Sometimes it just feels like they could be smarter. When there's a place that needs someone to build it, why not have someone automatically run towards it? Or towards burning houses?
So I don't know if this is a common known thing, but I can't kill enemy spies when they're discovering my lots
It just seems to annoy me, that they come up in the "jobless popup" above the builing options. Why not let them stay on hold?
Why not let people upgrade the city halls more often? And with advanced evolution add more buildings or other advantages maybe?
I don't know if thats just for me, but my game freezes for a couple of seconds when winter / summer arrives
But the thing that probably stuck in my head for the longest time now is the pace of the game. I'd love to play longer games with advanced infrastructure. Other than that, I really got to admit - for an alpha game, this is a beast!
I simply can't believe how much potential there is for this game! The game just has to get more in depth with infrastructure for example. I feel like this could become a game where even singleplayer will be fun for hours, just watching your civilization grow - fighting unknown creatures and / or enemies.
I had & will have a lot of fun playing this and might have missed out on some stuff or didn't get some things already in the game. Let me know please! After all, these were my thoughts after playing Northguard for the very first time :)

A while ago, I started playing Starbound. I got the best gear possible, and completed the game. I stopped playing it for a few months and forgot about it. Now, it's out of early access and I've already fallen in love with it again.
You'll see a lot of reviews saying how it's like "2D Minecraft" or "Terraria in space", but this game should not be rated comparatively to other games. Lots of time and effort was put into this game to make it a special and exceptional game. Do yourself a favor and buy it. However, unlike I said earlier, if you liked Terraria, give it a try. It's a similar concept with more advanced mechanics.
Side note: I'm glad we're experiencing the story's explanation now, instead of just starting on a half-destroyed ship.
Side-side note: When on the second bridge, grab the cape.

Main points (you decide if they're good or bad):
-Short (6-10 hours if you're familiar with point-and-click adventures)
-Dark.  Not scary, but images that are meant to be disturbing/unsettling.
-Story doesn't quite make sense and things are never really explained.  Good if you like coming up with your own theories, but bad if you wanted closure on characters/plot points.
-Puzzles are... adequate. 80% straightforward, 15% you can brute-force through by clicking/trying everything, 5% that you'll probably look up a guide online for because you missed something or didn't realize how to do something.
Overall I DO recommend the game, it was interesting, but I won't say it's a MUST-PLAY.  I think it could benefit from something that highlights clickable items (currently the only indicator is that the mouse icon changes on mouse-over).

The first thing that shows itself in Fran Bow is the love that its two creators have put into it.
The choice of genre may well be a case of 'knowing your limits', but it serves well, as the 2D interface complements the whimsical, childlike style of the narrative.
The art is amazing; I can't begin to imagine how much effort it took.
Puzzles are at a good difficulty but if you miss something in the room it can be frustrating. If you search everything and still find yourself very definitely stuck, searching the answer so that you can keep moving forward is perhaps better. The story is more the point of Fran Bow, rather than the individual puzzles.
On the other hand, the inventory commands can be counter-intuitive, for example, when fetching something for an NPC, simply talking to them with it in your inventory triggers a falsely negative response; one must 'use' the item on the character. While not a problem, it is not immediately obvious what you have to do.
One can very clearly see, seperate from the story, a change in atmosphere through each chapter. The simple gory horror of the beginning hospital develops and changes, partly affected by Fran's access to Duotine. Only the final chapter has an Alice in Wonderland theme, withe several intentional similarities and an explicit reference. While Fran Bow is very creepy in places, I would hesitate to classify it as a 'horror game'.
Lastly, the emotional journey is beautiful. Everything is through Fran's eyes; her confusion, her hope, her despair. Like her, the player is left wondering what is real and what is all in her head. I only wish there were multiple endings, as would have been possible. Still, 9/10, I will be playing it again.

Sleeping Dogs is everything I wanted from a GTA set in Hong Kong. If you wanted Infernal Affairs and a healthy sprinking of action from every Jackie Chan movie ever, this game is perfect!
The storyline is well written and impressively acted. You play as Wei Shen, an undercover cop, who needs to choose between loyalty to his new criminal brethren or to his duty as a police officer, people on both sides get suspicious, tense moments of untrustworthy accusations, etc. Kind of cliche, to be honest. If you've seen Infernal Affairs, or one of the many Hong Kong police dramas (or the US version The Departed) you have a general sense of what the story is about. Unfortunately the ending is a bit lackluster and you don't really get to make too many choices in the game. Nevertheless, it was interesting enough to keep me engaged for the 20 hour or so through the main storyline.
The more melee focused combat is something more akin to the Arkham series and is fun to enough to keep your interested through the entire game. There is some good ol' cover based shooting/ sweet slow motion but I felt like that was definitely the weakest part of the combat. You can do a bunch of badass♥♥♥♥♥♥like jack a car by jump from a moving car to another moving car so it's usually pretty fun to get into fights.
Sleeping Dogs unfortunately falls into the familiar trap of "Go here, beat up that guy", or "Go here and steal this car." that plague so many open world games. Still, the game is so cheap during sales these days, and the combat is so fun you'll find yourself walking around the streets just cruisin' for a bruisin'.
I'd highly recommend this is if you're into GTA or Action films in general, it's a lot of fun for the price and the DLCs can be some goofy fun.

Ever had a game that you didn’t really intend to play but did and in the end it was an amazing surprise? Developed by the amazingly named Shanghai “FantaBlade Network Technology Co., Ltd.” ICEY is a 2D hack and slash game that sees you pay ICEY a robot girl with a mission to kill Judas a being that is hellbent on… something…something bad… but in reality, this game is so much more than meets the eye.
A month ago I likened “One Night Stand” to a visual novel meets Stanley parable well this is a 2D hack and Slash meets Stanley Parable.
At its core, ICEY is an excellent 2D hack and slash with a fantastic combat system, excellent upgrades and a fantastic set of enemies to get your teeth into killing but what really makes this game stand out is the branching story with many different endings.
Like Stanley, Parable ICEY is a self-aware meta style game that has you follow (or not) the narrators commands you travel through the game. Replace first person walking sim with 2D hack and slash and you are pretty much there. Usually ignoring the narrator leads you up the garden path but sometimes it leads you to secret areas and interesting plot twists. The reality is that even though it took me about 2-3 hours to beat ICEY with one ending the reality is that there are so much more endings to go back and discover. In fact, the achievements in the game come from achieving multiple endings.
Graphics wise the game is beautiful to look at and the soundtrack is equally as awesome. What really makes it amazing is even without the Stanley Parable style narrator and story twists this would still be an excellent game but the interesting meta twists turn a great game into and the excellent one.
I really cannot recommend ICEY enough and I for one cannot wait for a sequel.

Great game for both Casual players and Hardcores!
Fun, simplistic gameplay and great graphics are tightly packed into something I thoroughly enjoyed and will continue to do so. I'm nowhere near done yet but seeing how reaching 100 % everywhere is going to take me a awhile (for achievements) I figured I'd give NEON DRIVE a quick thumbs up.
Here's a few suggestions I'd like to see if there's ever a continuation:
- Add FPS Cap other than VSYNC. A lot of PC players disable VSYNC because most of the time it just adds input delay, as have I. Instead I have capped the fps in my graphics card drivers manually but this option is something I would like to see in any game I play and most of the times it's not the case.
- Robot Voice that counts down 3, 2, 1.. after a Pause.
- Overview of position after Death. Too often I found myself blinking after hitting Continue and ended up driving into an obstacle. Sometimes this happened a couple of times in a row even. Maybe I'm just a dumb person though so take it with a grain of salt.
- Bonus Point modifier for avoiding Collisions - similar to Need For Speed series to promote reflexes rather than just  zooming down a lane and provide incentive to listen to the music and stay in beat as the Soundtrack is truly awesome. Might aswell add these modifiers in front of cars or slightly behind.

Mechanically solid. Netcode is pretty good, and crossplay with PS4 players gives this game longer life if you're playing online often. Some of my pros I also feel have cons to them as well. Also, I played majority of my time on the PS4 version before picking up the PC version so naturally the time I spent playing it on console isn't reflected in my time played on PC.
PROS
- Gameplay: The gameplay in my opinion is superb. It also feels smooth to play. I'm a fan of the the V-system though I do wish they a bit crazier with it.
- Direct Input Support - I play on a PS4/PS3 TE2 arcade stick so having this supported was crucial for me.
- Characters - I enjoy the characters in this roster. I feel like theres a good enough blend that any player can pick up someone who fits their playstyle.
- Training mode: Robust with plenty of options and the ability to record moves to the CPU character.
- Story mode: It's there
CONS
- Combos: I like that the combos are a bit easier to pull off than SF4 and the removal of focus attacks, but I feel like the combos don't really allow for creativity. You may see the same combos pulled off by the different people playing the same character. It just wish they allowed for a bit more creative freedom in what combos into what.
- Characters: I like the characters in the roster, but I feel like some of the characters need work. Balrog I feel needs to be nerfed a tad, and I feel like they need to add more characters that were staples to SF such as E Honda and Sagat. I don't play with either of them, but it just seems weird that they aren't in the game.
- Story mode: It's there now yes, but I was expecting more from it. It just ended up being a bit on the boring side. Juri is still bae though.
- Arcade mode: I'm still surprised there's no traditional arcade mode. No hitting barrels, no beating up a car. Disappointing.
- F2P features in what is considered a retail AAA game: Personally I can't stand this. I commend Capcom for letting all future DLC characters be earnable with in game currency, but the amount you get in in game currency for purchasing characters is basically a drip compared to how much they are. Initially you get most of your fight money from playing the character prequel stories and I think you also get them from completing challenges like survial mode and challenge mode. however once those dry up you can't go back to well for more fight money. You may get enough after this for a whopping 2 characters (maybe, I only had enough to get one and then buy some cosmetic items afterwards). Playing online and winning a match only nets you about 50 fight money, and completing challenges against players online will net you between 500 and 1,000 fight money. You also get 1,000 fight money each time you level up online. Meanwhile, characters are about 100,000 fight money, and stages can be around 70,000. Personally it bothers me and I think it's pretty scummy for a AAA that was available at full retail price would do something like this. In my opinion they should either lower the amount that each character and stage is worth or increase the amount you are able to earn in online matches to maybe 1,500 after each win, 2,000 for leveling up, and 1,000 for completing challenges during online matches. I think it would also be cool to see a money match where you can wager whatever amount of fight money you want in certain increments. That way they still get a revenue stream from people who may not want to spend the time trying to compete online and just buy the characters, and the players who fight online a lot don't feel like they are getting pennies per win online to then at some point finally get enough to buy a character because they don't want to spend more money on the game after already buying it. I could understand this for a F2P game, but for a game like Street Fighter, it just rubs me the wrong way. Again, kudos for making the characters earnable, but make it a bit easier to earn them because it's not like we didn't already spend money on the game game initally.
Anyway, if you're a casual player that doesn't care for playing online I still would not recommend the game because I still feel like the single player options are a bit undercooked. If single player is more secondary to you and you like to mainly hop online then I would say there's a lot here for you in regards to competive play, learning moves, and utilizing training mode quite a bit.

Don't let yourself fool by the screenshots. This isn't another one of those pretty yet repetative point&click adventures. This is the Story of Fran Bow. And it's intriguing. I never got that frightened by a point&click adventure. You think you have a clue about reality? This First person shooter game is quite an adventure after seeing all the alien,predator and the 2 alien vs predator movies I knew I had to get this game this game is quite unique from other first person shooters ive played, to begin there are 3 seperate campaigns Marine Alien and Predator each with 4 difficult settings Easy, Normal, Hard, and Nightmare
The first Campaign is the Marine this campaign is well in my opinion the longest but only bearly you start out with a flashlight and flares both are unlimited so dont be afraid to use flares if you get scared your go to weapon is your Pistal and for good reason its quite rapid fire and reguardless of difficulty unlimited Ammo for the Pistal, your other weapons include Pulse Rifle a Rapid fire mechine gun that also launches gernades, next we have the shotgun a devistateing weapon at close quarters but I do not recamend being that close to Alien if you head shot them their heads will release acid damage if your in Melee range, Next we have the flamethrower this has potential but I wasent that big of a fan of it mostly because Alien exploded each time I burned one, Next we have my absolute favorite the Sniper RIfle this monster can detect targets that you can even see yet includeing facehuggers still in their eggs and alien hideing in shadows or vents as well as Predators Cloak its somewhat rapid fire and stores alot of ammo, lastly we got the all powerful Smartgun this monster is a true demon it locks on to targets and like the Sniper rifle can detected targets you cant see yet it is extreamely rapid fire high ammo and possibly the strongest weapon in the game for this reason I listed it last, you are also equiped with a motion sensor both watch and listen to it will tell you if a enemy is near only if its movieng around but it wont tell you if its above or below you
Now the Marine Campaign is filled with absolute horror it took me 7 attempts to complete the first mission thats because everytime I saw the motion sensor go off I would quit out of fear eventually I Faught past the fear and finished the storyline, as the Marine you will face off against numerous aliens (also known as Serpents) Facehuggers (these little demons I still fear to this day the good thing about the game is they dont just rush you they move like 5 yards in some direction then stop for like 3 sec then move again gives you plenty of time to shoot them do not fear if they try to latch on to your face your charcter will block and you will take some damage but it wont kill you) Next we have combate androids these things take a few hits to bring down and headshots dont kill them Lastly you will face one Predator in the game my advice Line of sight him if you see the triple Red beam and dont forget to block
Next is the Alien Campaign this is the shortest you will use Darkness to your advantage any chance you get destroy the lights it will make detecting you alot harder, on them keep in mind Aliens mobility is completely unmatched you can hide in vents while your health regenerates if you get low and Alien can walk on any surface Alien will face Marines Combat Androids and Predators
Lastly we have my favorite Campaign Predator he is basicly a hybrid of both Races extreamely deadly physical and ranged weapons He also has Cloaking abilitys makeing him 90% invisible he can also distract Marines to wander off he also is able to make increadible jumps his mobility is Secound to Alien he also has the most health his campaign starts out hard but as you get more sub weapons the game gets easier, your sub weapon list goes as follows Plasma Caster this is the default ranged weapon charged shots deal extreame damage but cost more energy non charged stun the target temperarally, Proximity Mines these are useful for laying traps they are extreamely explosive once you arm one never go near it again this weapon also consumes Power to use, Smart Disk this is extreamely effective at takeing out serpents on walls the disk will follow your triple red Laser and come back after about 5 secounds, and Combi Spear this is my favorite weapon they have it takes careful aim but if you hit its instant death to all but bosses  note the Triple Laser used but the Plasma Caster and the Smart Disk Humans can track you once you use it the Proximity mines Smart Disk and Combi Spear can be used while cloaked and it wont Decloak you the Plasma Caster will though, as the campaign continues he will gain access to a new Predator mask that not only allows himt to see human heat signatures but also Aliens as they stalk the darkness his mask also has a zoom option as well is recieveing detailed information about the target hes looking at such as their ranged and melee damage output and what species they are, the Predator Campaign is my favorite because of all the options at your disposal
To summerize this game was absolutely amazing and im glad I bought it.

is a sort of hybrid action side-scroller "beat 'em up" style game with a narration that guides you along, if you so choose to follow.  The choices you make will change what happens, and you can discover some interesting extras by doing things differently than you are asked by the narrator of the story, kind of in a similar way to something like The Stanley Parable.
When you start out, you are asked a series of questions, and these questions will determine your difficulty.  I only played this game on easy, and even died one time I think, so I'd imagine some of the higher difficulties could be pretty challenging.  I don't really generally play harder difficulties unless I have a reason to, since I prefer for things to move along, and I can get frustrated easily.  It's a relative term anyway, since some people are better at certain genres, and might prefer more challenge.
The first thing I noticed when I began playing was the fluidity of movement, and the flashy graphics.  I had a lot of fun exploring and using various moves and such as I got going.  The narration is very busy in this game, and it can be pretty fun discovering secrets or finding extra money in various nooks and crannies while progressing.  There are auto-save points with little stations that you can buy upgrades to your moves as you collect more money, giving it a very light RPG element as well.  Some spots will create teleports (though I don't know exactly when they are created until I check through the menu).  You can go back and re-battle things for more money, and collect the same special gold stash spots over and over, if you wish.
The narration is nice, and keeps it interesting as you are moving from spot to spot.  There is some humor as you move forward (or choose not to), especially if you decide to disobey the voice.  I was reminded of a lot of things that were very similar to some of the situations in The Stanley Parable, for instance.
I used a controller, and the confirm and back/cancel buttons were reversed, but when I switched controller schemes in the menu (from PS to XBOX), it seemed to make it normalized for me, so I didn't have to really adjust, but I do remember other games where I had to do this same kind of thing on occasion.  I was extremely impressed with the responsiveness on this game.  I find myself having some gripes with many platformers or fighting or action games where sometimes the timings won't always fire off with the right precision, but not once in this game did I notice anything like that happening.
The story is a bit of a reference to The King in Yellow, but I cannot really comment a lot on this, since I haven't read it.  The plot itself is pretty interesting, since it seems to be layered, with the underlying narration and sub-plot sort of thing going on.  It is intriguing, and I think it does accentuate and make the overall experience better.
It seemed a little bit short, or maybe I just got very absorbed in gameplay, since I finished the entire game in two split sessions.  Something that keeps me playing is definitely a plus as well.  I'm trying to think of any negatives besides the overall length, but it's not very easy to really do.  The game is great, and I think most people would really really enjoy this.
Very nice graphics, and a smooth and bright look to everything.  Characters, bosses, enemies, and environments are extremely well done, and solid.
The music has the techo kind of feel, which works with the overall setting of the game.  It's a little strong, but it fits the game style very well in various areas of travel.
Fluid movements with controller.  I really have to give this the highest mark I can as far as that part goes.  Great responsiveness!
Fun mechanics with fighting.  Damaging the bots and then breaking cores to regenerate, then using chains off of those was entertaining, and helps if there is a momentary lapse or struggle in the fights.  I like the flow and balance as I played.
The narration aspect is a great touch.  It makes it stand out from the average action game, since there is an extra voice that accompanies you as you travel around.  Some nice gags and other humor as you make varied choices with progression.  There are a lot of little hidden things one would miss if they treated it as a straight linear adventure.  Most just unlock achievements, but they are fun to find, nonetheless, and add some depth to the overall gameplay from this standpoint.
Maybe one or two spots with grammatical errors, but they are not glaring.  I do not even recall what they were, but one near the beginning, and one towards the end is all I caught.
I would have liked this to be a bit longer, since it was such a good game to play.  Everything I did spend time on was quality though, so it's hard to really complain about it.  I would have liked the price to be a few dollars less due to the amount of time I spent, or have a little more content.
Some extra enemy types would have been good to throw in the  mix.  Small gripe, but I have to try to find something I'd like changed up.  What was done is very good though, and the bosses are all unique.
I would have liked a manual save.  I don't think there was a way to do this in the game.
Maps are great.  I almost always like maps.  This wasn't too crazy though, and it's not something you'd get lost in, by any means.  Pretty straight-forward, as far as that goes.
Anyone who likes hybrid games, and fans of The Stanley Parable might enjoy this quite a bit.  The action and fighting elements are fun with this game.  This is not a metroidvania, as is listed in the tags on Steam!  Progression feels smooth as you move through the story, and there are not any real hiccups or lulls.  As mentioned above, the controls are great, the narration is a nice touch, and I would have a hard time being critical of much on this game.
Almost anybody who likes this general style of game really should play this.  I'm extremely satisfied with my experience on the game.  It has made me pause a bit and think about things overall as well with my own self.

Fallout 4 has way better graphics than earlier Fallout games which is great but makes the game require higher specs to run it well. Fallout games are shouldn't require too high specs The new settlement building function is nice and I can spend a lot of time with settlement building. I like Fallout 4 but it feels different compared to earlier Fallout games because of many new things introduced and changed. I had to get a new PC to be able to play the game well enough but I can/could run any earlier Fallout game well with my older PC.
I definitely recommend this game to any Fallout fan and people who like post-apocalyptic games.

I think one of the major problems with this game in general is the fact that it doesn't even play or feel like a doom game at all, which is present in Doom 3 already. The horror aspect of Doom 3 is welcome, but at the same time the white-knuckle high speed action and mowing down hundreds and hundreds of demons is gone.  I am in no way trying to sound like a Classic Doom Purist but Doom 3 is just a huge departure from the original formula because most game sequels should tend to build on it's previous part and make things better.   Doom 3 didn't do that.  BFG edition?  It's debatable.
This package here is an "enhanced" edition of Vanilla Doom 3 with 2 expansions, Ressurection of evil, which is the same thing except some new weapons and an artifact that grants you temporary powers depending on the upgrades you got from defeating any of the special barons of hell, and a grabber gun which works like the gravity gun from Half life 2, except lets go of the item when it's core heats up too much.   there is also a second expansion which tries to raise the number of monsters to fight at a gfiven time like the original games but still fail at that anyway because this game is primarily a horror survival shooter, and that's where Doom 3 fails to ressurect the original formula of just gunning hundreds and hundreds of ♥♥♥♥ing demons.
The other expansion, "Lost Mission"  was to answer what happened to Bravo team during the events of Doom 3.  It's basically trying to go back to the original game's roots of the series by adding more monsters to kill but somehow still fail to execute just that.  It's still a horror survival.  ♥♥♥♥ that.  I want hundreds of ♥♥♥♥ing demons to kill, not just 2 or 5 at a time in each room.
As far as graphics go, It still looks the same as vanilla doom except it looks alot clearer but even so, there doesn't seem to be much fix on lighting, for instance, your wepaon doesn't even flash in the dark despite the muzzle blasts coming out of your guns.  As a matter in fact, the imp's fireballs are the only few things that glow in the dark....seriously.
Another controversial addition is now a flashlight that's mounted on your armor instead of a hand held flashlight like in Vanilla Doom 3, which was a welcome in my opinion because if Doom 3 was supposed to be more like the classic games and not a horror survival, this was one of the steps to go with it and that was fine.  I wanted to kill♥♥♥♥♥♥ not walk around in the dark waiting to get my♥♥♥♥♥♥slashed off by a hell knight standing 4 feet infront of me while walking blindly in the darkness.  ♥♥♥♥ that.
Both of the Classic Doom games comes with the package as a selection before Doom 3's menu.  Only changes are the graphics on the healthpacks which now shows a pill and adolf hitler's Wolfenstien 3d's portrait was also removed to get this game not banned in Germany.
Mutliplayer is completely dead, which isn't really a highlighted mode in Doom 3, but in my opinion, it's way better than Doom 2016's sad garbage excuse of a multiplayer game, but that's exacly why the arena fps died out because games today got really soft in the multiplayer department and Doom 2016's multiplayer proves that.  as a result, all the Call of duty/Destiny players flock over to Doom 4 and are like "holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ this is PHENOMINAL!"   Because that game, even with's multiplayer totally resonates with that kind of crowd, but not Doom 3...no.   hahaha.  no.
though the modes are just straight up deathmatch, teamdeathmatch, CTF, Tournament which is just Duel i think, everyone spawns in the arena with the same loadout, SMG with 150 rounds left over, so you just find weapons, armor, health and frag it out to the death, and that is something that the newer audiences of today's gaming couldn't handle 5 minutes thrown into the map with other higher skilled players. no loadouts, No perks, no hack mods, no powersuits, no demon runes that help you gain powers and one shot everything.  just pure skill, map knowledge----yep, those days are long gone.
On a fair note, even Vanilla Doom 3 was already lackluster compared to other popular shooters at the time such as Halo 2 on the xbox console and it's critically claimed multiplayer mode which was it's other highlight and even Half life 2 at the time.  One thing they did right in this version is the amounts of health, ammo cache locations are doubled so you got tons of ammo, so that means less time looking around the area for ammunition and more time shooting demons, which is good but even so with how the levels are set up in this game, there would hardly be any room to circle strafe around your enemies and kill them.  Also, the monster ratio is doubled.  It seems they tried to make this game more like it's original counterparts, which is good but It just wasn't enough in the end.
Is the game worth it?  maybe.  Depends on what you're looking for, honestly.  I'd rather just wait to see if this game goes on sale.  If not, don't touch this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ until then.  This♥♥♥♥♥♥ain't Doom.

Windscape is an ambitious title that looks to mix the old parts of games you love with the new trends of today. One part Zelda, two parts Elder Scrolls is a good way to sum up the formula for Windscape. Developer Magic Sandbox aims to accomplish this gargantuan goal in simple ways. However, filling the Steel Boots of these epic titles is far from an easy task and drowning in a Lake Hylia is more then likely if one doesn't tread carefully.
From the onset Windscape is doing rather well for itself, currently in its early development stage. The moment you load up into the game your eyes are overwhelmed by the bright colorful world. Aesthetically, Windscape aims to have simple graphics, reminiscent of the classic Ocarina of Time but with more of clean crisp look. Needless to say, but the game is extremely polygonal, The people, monsters, caves, mountains, clouds, everything is polygons. At first this is going to take some adjustment, at least for me it did. Once you do adjust though you realize how beautiful the game looks with its vibrant tones.
Deeper areas of the Early Access show the versatility of this art style, as everything goes from bright and cheery to dark and sinister. I personally can't wait to see what future areas are going to be like and how far this style can go. Other aspects shine as well, such as level design, use of lighting and particle effects. There are some areas for improvement of course. The UI needs improvement, house designs become repetitive, and other little things here and there.
Another highlight we should talk about is the music of Windscape. As soon as you embark on your adventure you are greeted by a soundtrack full of levity and excitement. The tracks capture perfectly the inspiration for the game but doesn't feel copied nor does it drag at any point. It's definitely one of the areas I enjoyed most about Windscape. I could just sit there and enjoy the music for quite a bit. In short, the developer has nailed the overall feeling of the game and just needs to keep moving forward and keep things interesting.
Touching upon those Elder Scroll elements, we have the first person combat and crafting. Windscape takes the scheme of other survival crafting titles and simplifies most of it. Unlike in Zelda, here you can craft your own weapons and tools to use in combat. As of right now there are spells, bows, blunt weapons, and sharp weapons, all corresponding with a different damage stat.
How this is going to be expanded upon will be interesting to see, as there is no hunger bar or really any other survival mechanics outside of your health bar. While crafting in the game is simple, it ended up feeling a little bit like a chore for me. It especially sapped the joy out of opening huge treasure chests. which usually just contained materials to craft something or meat. So much meat. Crafting materials tend to pile up.
The reason it felt like a chore is because the combat is rather simple and easy to exploit.(Of course that will likely change) Using saving totems automatically refills your health, so items such as food or health potions only become necessary on rare occasion. The resistance to damage type potions, I never used once, despite them being a huge chunk of crafting. The crafting system though does have plenty of room to grow in good ways, from crafting armor, shields, and magic accessories. The only problem is going to be making it fun and exciting.
Combat is great but does suffer from quite a few bugs, AI randomly going brain dead and standing still, little variation in tactic beyond just charging up a shot, hitting and backing off. It becomes a very much rinse and repeat scenario. Situational awareness is an issue with no HUD as well. Boss fights on the other hand, when they do work, feel like epic show downs. You gotta move fast and play smart as they have far superior health and damage.
With currently about two whole areas to explore, you will get about four hours out of the game. That is stretching it if you want to craft everything. Obviously more content is on the way with a plethora of changes. I can see why people are excited about Windscape, the game does have plenty of potential, but it needs to build on itself in a pretty massive epic way. There are areas that need some tender loving care such as combat, bugs, AI. Ideas that can bring more life to the game such as voice acting, personal housing, and what I loved most of all about Ocarina of Time mini-games and secrets around every corner!
At $16.99 currently, keep in mind purchasing this title is mostly to SUPPORT THE DEVELOPER, as there is hopefully way more content coming. Given the developers constant updates, great publisher and passionate game intro, from the developer on the Steam page, I wouldn't worry about the game being completed. So keep your eyes on this one as it grows into a classic for sure.
