So I've played the series since 09' like many with Street Fighter 4, I played that game competitively in Philadelphia at most of the Big E tournaments, and I play ST, 3S, SFxT, and other fighting games since I started back then, all pretty well.
This game is a good fighting game, but I don't recommend this game for everyone, here's why.
If you're playing strictly online and you're not living in a populated area, you're going to have a hard time playing. The game does allow you to filter online opponents up to 5 bar connections, but it doesn't allow you to region lock and the filtration system isn't as good as it looks, you will get people up to two bars lower than the setting you get. You might see 5 bars on the screen, but you'll enter the match and they will still lag like a 3 bar. Setting the game to 5 bars also reduces the uptime on matches by a decent amount, where you may wait up to 5 minutes per new opponent online.
Another thing to mention that unlike other fighting games, this one in particular is mechanically designed to reward offense rather than neutral game and defense. They implimented a 6.5 input delay for moves in the game, so even if you see many moves coming, when you react the game doesn't register until over a 10th of a second to your input to defend yourself, combine that with common online lag, and the most successful play style for a player to win with online at home is pressure, just constant pressure.
To really enjoy this game and fighting games in general you really need to find people to play with offline and sit side by side with them on the same screen. This is the last genre to really do that, unlike our old consoles of the past, maybe Nintendo will keep the side by side gaming style alive, but this is it. You won't enjoy this game unless you learn how to play it well, being able to execute combos given an opportunity is something that comes only from practice, and getting those opportunities only comes with experience.
If you're new to the series, this is a great title.
It's a blast to play, but if you just mash, you won't really get your moneys worth.

While I haven't played Starbound in ages, I can certainly say that this game had a lot of potenial when it first went into early access. Those intial days of those first updates were fun and brought us new features. I thought this game was going to be a rival of Terraria and I was honeslty surprised in the differences that I saw in the early stages, but then...
Chucklefish went MIA for a long time. The game got stale, bugs weren't getting fixed, and now almost three years later it's getting released.
While I can't say that I didn't enjoy the game and what I've played, and I loved it every bit of it, I can't recommend this game only for the the devs. I've been with the community almost since the beginning and I had a lot of hopes for this game like a lot of the community. While I can't speak for everyone I'm displeased at how Chucklefish worked on this game and how they treated the community, I'm not going to throw and shade but I need to be careful of what I say because of acts they've done in the past to people talking about Starbound. I am however going to make a pro and con list of the games feautes and what's made it the experience that is it.
-Large variety of blocks to build with
-Fun and inviting landscapes
-Wide variety of weapons to kill, maim, and destroy with
-Seven playable races
-Soothing OST
-Easy to pick up combat system
-Game's Purpose: Building is fun if you're creative.
-Beginning is boring, mid-game is boring, everything just tends to be "boring." The game tends to just be a huge collect-a-thon
-Boss fights. Let me expand on this first: The boss fights just aren't interesting. The first boss you fight is just bland and not enjoyable, the rest of the bosses are slighltly different, but not as fun.
-Optimization (I still don't understand HOW this game isn't optimized. It still gets lag spikes even though my computer runs hardware that's a lot faster than the recommended specs. I know not every game is perfect, but I shouldn't lag everytime I enter my ship or go into a menu. This game honeslty is just poorly optimized and Chucklefish should have fixed that a long time ago.)
-Quests and NPCs aren't fun to do or interact with; most quests are fetch quests or a "Do this to complete a query so I can give you an item that's already out classed by experience." While there are a lot of quests in Starbound, most of them are needed to progress in the "story," and just take too much time to do. NPCs are still basic and uninteresting. Nothing has changed since the first update, they still just say a few lines and walk around.
-The "Story:" There's a forced story in this game and while some say it's a good way to teach players, it's just so slow paced that it hinders the experience. When I started playing Starbound it was just "Build and survive," but now that there's a story that is REQUIRED TO ADVANCE IN ANY TECHNOLOGICAL WAY it honestly just makes the game more of a chore.
-Game's Purpose: If you aren't a creative person, this game just lacks much of anything for you.
-Planets: They're all just color swaps with different environments. The generation is lacking, and in some cases is down right unfair, I.E. Huge death pit that you won't find until your mining durasteel or slime biomes that just make you bounce into enemies
I can't hate this game. I liked it for what it was when it was a lot more basic, but with all these additions Chucklefish keeps bringing in, it's honestly making the game more of a chore. I can't recommend this game only because of how slow development was and how the devs treated the community, especially during the hiatus. While it is getting released, FINALLY, in a few days (Or is released if you're reading this review on release day,) it's not worth the money.
While I don't hate this game, I just wish that the whole development cycle would have gone differently and I hope that the release changes how the devs produce for the community and interact with the community.
Until these changes, please don't get this game.

Games of Glory isn't a simple MOBA, for having played at every major games of this kind (DoTA, DoTa II, LoL, HoN, SMITE, HoTS...) I can tell the only game I found such original, deep and crazy experience is GoG.
Gameplay: In a MOBA gameplay is kinda straightforward, or it is?
Usually you have to use your mouse, right clicking on the place to go, right clicking on the ennemy to auto attack... well not that much exciting isn't it?
In GoG there is no such thing as an Auto Attack and you can move via mouse click or with WASD (yup this looked strange too me also, but this gives trully new gaming perspectives).
Let's talk about maps, here we have 2 different maps with two TOTALLY different game modes and ways to play, one "classic" defend base -but with some new shiny ideas such as capture the point income and victory point- and one "protect the VIP" objective.
This gives more deepness to the game since you have to rethink how to use your clone (champion) and build!

Fran Bow isn't for everyone, but if you are looking for a unique experience, look no further. This game did a fantastic job at keeping me guessing & trying to make connections throughout the game. I was constantly struggling to determine what was reality and what was imagination. As soon as I thought I had my footing, the game would pull it out from under me again. Fran Bow is a surreal psychological horror game that I will never forget.
To describe the gameplay, it is a point-and-click puzzle game of sorts, broken into chapters. Unlike some point-and-clicks I have played, the puzzles in Fran Bow are usually sensical, given the world that they occur in. I love most games that are twisted and dark, so Fran Bow is right up my alley.

Town of Salem has easily become one of my favorite online games of all time. It reminds me of other popular party games such as Mafia or Werewolf, but way more organized and with better mechanics. There's light role-playing involved to figure out who's who, and the ability to take notes and leave wills contributing to someone getting lynched are all for the purpose of winning the game.
Whether you're a Townie, Mafia, or some other non-denominational job you'll have different objectives to complete in order to win. You are randomly assigned a role each game, given only a text box telling what your abilities are, and how you win. The best part about this is you don't have to be alive in order to win all the time. As long as the townies win, every townsperson killed in the process wins too. You can even contribute information to your team after death by talking to a Medium who can relay that information to the living.
Online matches are very quick and easy to understand, and the game sounds more complicated that it really is. Every game offers a new experience in terms of 14 other new players to communicate with, and plenty of opportunities for alliances or role swaps. If you like RPG elements, mixed with a board game atmosphere about a murder mystery, this game is worth checking out.
If you don't want to buy it, it is free to play at
Though buying the Steam version comes with perks such as faster loading times, better compatibility with operating systems, achievements, and $5 worth of town coins used to customize your character.

This is a very tricky review to write.
On the positives, there is genuine intrigue and mystery (particularly in the first couple of chapters), some interesting spooky characters, great animation and cut scene sequences, some good scares and some fairly decent puzzles in the mix.
On the negatives, that's 9 hours of my life that I'm not getting back.
I don't want to give anything away in this review but there is a serious point where they drop the ball on both the story line and my interest. I really had to drag myself through chapter three to five.
It starts out very true to the Steam adverts/clips with the very creepy asylum and the strong beginnings of a mystery, where you're ultimately trying to work out if she is traumatised and innocent or psychotic and guilty.
It then swiftly evolves into something that reminded me very much of when a child is trying to describe their dream from the night before ("and then this happened, and this strange character was there....").
There were some genuinely good escape room puzzles in this, but then there was a whole chapter of irratingly (and needlessly) long winded chapters. On a whole it felt like they were trying to mix several short escape games into one, with each chapter feeling more rushed and thrown together than the last. I enjoyed the mini games that broke up the chapters although I thought they were not in keeping with the main game itself.
I would not reccommend this game, unless you were interested in playing the first two chapters only.

is 'arcade'-like, albeit to a fault. It is 'arcade' in that gameplay is shallow and controls are simple; the first minute of play is probably pretty similiar to the tenth hour of play. Admittedly because of what I just mentioned, I do generally have a biased against 'arcade'-like games to begin with, but as long as they have addictive gameplay with a fairly novel mechanic - we get along well.
The worst part about this title is the penalty for messing up. The difficulty setting determines how many chances to keep going; on 'hard' I believe you have one single chance and then it's a forced restart. I think a better system would be like in the other rhythym based games I named, where you have some sort of score that is penalized, but you keep going. This way it isn't just 'pass' or 'fail' - which is a frustrating system that just isn't all that fun.
+Music and artwork are cool
-Wasted potential with a poorly designed score system; they should have taken notes from the giants that have already figured out how to do rhythym-based mechanics
-Failure is frustrating, and there is nothing pulling me back in
-Yes, I could just 'git gud' at this title, or simply dump dozens of hours into a much more established and wayyy better music based game such as

Playing as the alien is mostly a stealth affair where you attract the marines with your hiss and kill them viciously with your jaws. It is I think the easiest campaign, because of the regenrating health of the alien and the fact that you stay hidden most of the time in tunnels and have excellent capability of clinging to most surfaces in any orientation.
The predator campaign starts as somewhat quirky becaue you are mostly limited to melee options as your weapons need to be charged from energy sources and deplete pretty quickly, but once you get the last 2 weapons, you are a powerhouse. You get the thermal vison for humanoid enemies and alien vision for the aliens. The best part about playing as alien is again the viciousness with which you kill the humans (such as yanking their heads out) as well the utter helplessness of an alien once you hold it in your hands (after knocking it down).
I took about 12 hours to complete all the campaigns on Hard difficulty, which is a decent amount of time. Considering that the game is often available for $3.75 on steam during sales, there no reason why you shouldn't buy it unless you don't like shooter games.

I went into this game a little iffy, but over all i found the experience to be extremely satisfying. It is essentially 3 games in one and lets you experience the same two or three days as a human marine, a predator or an alien. Without spoiling what happens, what is most interesting is that the storyline assumes you (the player) are playing each faction at once and therefore all factions kind of win. Within context of the story, you'll understand and it makes perfect sense. But lets break down the 3 games you get:
Marine: Storywise this is the most rich and fulfilling of all three factions. You learned the most about what is happening and why. Gameplay-wise it is a bit clunky. As a "shooter" it does very few things right but accomplishes well enough for you to get along. Controls all need to be remapped but still remain clunky. Weapons seem to lack "umph" where you'd expect it. And movement... ugh, its bad. Livable, but bad.
Alien: There isn't much of a story here.. i mean there is a little but it is minimal. Oddly, where the Marine experience went foul (movement) the Alien play-through does remarkably well. You can crawl and jump on all surfaces and combat feels very fluid, if not a little tough to get used to. Hunting humans is an absurd amount of fun in this mode and when you need to hunt a predator you notice a stark difference in how powerful you are. Hint: you aren't.
Predator: Storyline here is really intriguing...but too short, i feel like. This is mainly due to the fact that we know literally nothing about this faction from any of the movies. As such you're left hungering for it if you like the franchise. Sadly this title doesn't answer many questions but the story is really good. Gameplay is by far my favorite. The predator is tanky, stealthy and hunts both the humans and aliens extremely effectively. My only complain is there isn't enough of it.
Overall there is maybe too much gametime dedicated to the Humans compared to the Alien and Hunter factions. Realistically, you're only playing this to play as one of these two since there are a billion marine shooter games out there. That experience is really only worthy of a really well made cutscene to get all that juicy storyline in. Although its playable, you won't have nearly as much fun as playing as predator or aliens. I recommend saving the marine for last since you'll actually want the full story by the time you finish the other play-throughs. That desire will help you through any clunkiness in the gameplay.
Over all a great game. The 3 factions concept is well executed and feels really nice. You leave the game really understanding what was happening on this rogue planet. You may not understand the backstory of any faction, but you know why everything is happening in this small colony and that is something rare in games or literature. It is a very fulfilling experience.

Cons:
- Still no subtitles.

Overall Rating: 8.2/10,  Super Street Fighter IV rating back in it's day: 10/10
Although I prefer Street Fighter 5 for it's classic feeling gameplay, graphics, updates and active player base.
Give SFV another chance. It's really improved lately and especially since June 2016 although I didn't notice all the big changes until April of this year I reccomend it especially at it's $20 sale price right now although $40 is still a bargain to be playing Street Fighter's latest entry
Street Fighter Fan;
Online Play 9/10 - As good as Ultra, imo.
Modes Options Features 9/10 - You can turn the effects off and AA off similar to adjusting SFIV's graphics to your liking, training is pretty detailed too which is important and it has a better match finder features than the previous title as well I believe.
Story mode 9/10 - The best story mode in a Street Fighter to date, although it isn't a challenge which is good you'll need the funds to buy %30 of your first character
Graphics / Animations 8/10 - They're better than 4, but we still need to see Sakura to fully approve of the animation department, I don't find myself missing the awesome Ink effect of Street Fighter 4. The graphics are so detailed in some areas that it would look out of place. There's some low res textures on the PC version where they're not required, our PC's could have handled more. Also there are 3d modeled cloth pieces that clip into character models especially during Story Mode, SSF4 and USF4 deviantart fans fixed this issue in the past with mods.
Characters 8/10 - The characters that are here are good and I'm glad it isn't packed with boss characters like IV got packed with over it's various iterations. Bison, Urien and Necali are enough in that manner imo. It's missing Sakura which is the reason I really got hooked on the series, it's a shame but I've found other characters fun such as Cammy, Rog, Ryu and Juri. Ryu is really close to Sakura combo wise imo but nowhere near the animation brilliance of USF4.
Theme 6.9/10 Isn't very memorable but I went back and listened to the older OSTs and with the newer updates the music of this release as grown on me while some of the theme does need adjustment like "General Story Mode" - Isn't very tasteful of a naming convention. The main menu is a bit generic and targeted at eSports, you should never target your game at eSports it should be a by - product of the game. Sure you can put camera and viewing features in that's fine but don't dull down the artistic menus and neat features of Street Fighter X Tekken and Street Fighter 4 in favor of generic eSports oriented bull.
Combos: 6/10 I still feel they should be a bit easier like 5 frames like they originally promised. I'm having a hell of a time learning new combos and I've got a lot of unsucessful hours into these games and a mean Sanwa fight stick. The hardest combos are now 3 frames instead of 1 but I remember them saying 5? I guess I should see just how much damage I would be missing out on by going with all 5 frame combos if that's even possible. 60fps, 3 frames of 1 second I mean that window is so ridiculous why not increase it to 5, it would still feel like street fighter wouldn't it? Mortal Kombat and KI's tolerance is upwards of 1/3rd(20frames) of a second I believe? This is just irritating how tough they make the combos and doesn't promote new professionals or good fundamentals it just promotes top tier characters, no lifers and people who play 24/7 to get rank 1 online when you do silly choices like this. Wether the pros realise it or not they're dropping attacks or doing some of the more easier ones rather than getting that extra 20 damage and risk thinking about dropping an attack.
DLC, Microtransactions: 10/10 - Saves time to buy your character then you can either buy stages or costumes with your fight money. I didn't buy the DLC but I see the price and the time you'll save instantly getting the characters that would normally be packaged with Super, Arcade and Ultra. For a person with the budget and wanting to increase thier knowledge of characters its a bargain, actually doing characters inputs yourself helps you know the character you are fighting more quickly than guides and watching SFV.

Am I somehow expected to believe that the story, which is at the moment nothing more than the narrator telling me to go left or right and having random screens popup at gameplay, will spontaniously go into something extravagant and extreme and fun to play? Will it become something that will take my eyes away from the less-than-resposive combat, boring and lifeless tone, and uncohesive game I'm trying to play and turn it into a masterpiece?
Maybe it's a niche game, but I can call out a fair handful of games, sidescrollers even, that can capture your attention right off the bat and still retain that awesome flair throughout the experience.

Town of Salem has easily become one of my favorite online games of all time. It reminds me of other popular party games such as Mafia or Werewolf, but way more organized and with better mechanics. There's light role-playing involved to figure out who's who, and the ability to take notes and leave wills contributing to someone getting lynched are all for the purpose of winning the game.
Whether you're a Townie, Mafia, or some other non-denominational job you'll have different objectives to complete in order to win. You are randomly assigned a role each game, given only a text box telling what your abilities are, and how you win. The best part about this is you don't have to be alive in order to win all the time. As long as the townies win, every townsperson killed in the process wins too. You can even contribute information to your team after death by talking to a Medium who can relay that information to the living.
Online matches are very quick and easy to understand, and the game sounds more complicated that it really is. Every game offers a new experience in terms of 14 other new players to communicate with, and plenty of opportunities for alliances or role swaps. If you like RPG elements, mixed with a board game atmosphere about a murder mystery, this game is worth checking out.
If you don't want to buy it, it is free to play at
Though buying the Steam version comes with perks such as faster loading times, better compatibility with operating systems, achievements, and $5 worth of town coins used to customize your character.

BUT... playing it on my own, is a completely different beast.
I am VERY impressed by this game. I know it had a genuinely BAD initial release. It insultingly lacked content and I fully agreed with all the negatives that Capcom received from basically rushing the game out of the doors just because they wanted it to be officially available (and "viable") for Tournaments which at the time were closing in really fast. They should NOT have done that... but now it's too late and the damage has been done. It's SO unfortunately that SFV is mostly being remembered for that, instead of being appreciated for what it is NOW.
As I said, I'm not Street Fighter franchise "fan", and certainly not a veteran. I do know that - apparently so anyway - the most popular ones in the franchise are, in fact, the older titles still to this day. Such as the oh-so classic and still very much working and viable SF2 Turbo, or Alpha 2, or even the highly technical / complex Alpha 3 (I've read that Alpha 3 is still to this day the most complex and difficult-to-master Street Fighter in the entire franchise), or the nearly-perfected and fine-tuned Third Strike (the animations quality for a game that's made out of sprites is absolutely stunning to me). And I also often read that even SF4 is "better" than SF5. But then again, I usually realize that most of the 'negative' views about SF5 STILL stem from the failed and rushed nature of the initial release. But what about the actual CORE fighting of the game itself? How IS SF5 as an actual fighting game? Well I'm asking... but in reality I don't really care since I'm no veteran of the franchise anyway, but I do appreciate a quality versus quanity game any time of the day, regardless of the genre.
I've just started to play SF5 and after just one and a half day of play there's obvious high-quality stuff that jumps at me right from the start:
+ The animations (and animation transitions) in this game are STUNNING. It's so... how can I put it... "organic"? "Natural"? It's like there's a 100 "extra" frames of animations for small details on all body parts of every characters. If I compare SF5's animations to... say... Killer Instinct's or MKX's the one word that comes to mind is "stiffness", or "frames" (or lack thereof). In favor of SF5, there seems to be more frames, it's just smooth. When something as simple as a character stands back up after being knocked down he doesn't just nearly 'appear' standing up after like 2 frames like you'd see in Killer Instinct (one example I can think of in KI is the standing up animation for Glacius, one moment he's lying flat on the ground and the next moment the transition of him standing up is literally composed of something like 3 frames, it's ugly to look at).
Anyway I don't have the technical terms to talk about this aspect in details, especially if there's actual animators reading this. But as a gamer who appreciates smooth animations in fighting games all I can say is that as far as 3D / polygonal-based fighting games go (I'm excluding 2D / sprite-based ones since they're on their own class) SFV is quite literally the best one I've seen to this day. If one day they make SF6 I can only hope that they keep the same animation team.
+ The music is good! What else can I say? It's memorable, it's not irritating to the point where I feel like I should turn it off, and it seems to fit this game in general like fitting a pair of gloves. In other words it's good enough to leave it on while I play (contrarily to the music in the MK franchise which I usually turned off in order to listen to my own playlist in the background).
+ The pacing, in general, is right where I like it. It's not too fast, but not too slow. To me what's important in a fighting game is when the speed at which the characters move and execute their special moves is "slow enough" for me to 1) See it coming, and 2) Anticipate what the other player is trying to do because not only the animations show it to start with but the speed isn't too high in order for me to have the time to REACT to whatever is on its way. I've seen faster-paced games and they're usually too difficult for me. There's other perhaps better examples but immediately I can think of Killer Instinct here. I actually DO really like Killer Instinct... BUT... that game IS fast-paced compared to SF5. I do not mind fast-paced fighting games in general but I just happen to suck at them as a result. A fighting game does not have to be fast-paced to be "complex" or "competitive-friendly", in my book. So yeah I think that SF5's general character movement and moves execution speed is just right where it should be (at least for me... because some people said that SF5 is actually too slow for a SF game).
+ Characters, and character design. By that I mean I love the characters that they added (after release, but also including the default ones at release) and I just love how they are rendered under this new (UE4) engine. Now I too also REALLY love sprites and 2D or 2.5D fighting games. I LOVE how Third Strike is animated and presented in general, or Alpha 3 as well (just speaking visually here, animations, art / pixels-style, etc). But when it comes to the 3D and polygonal field of visuals then OH BOY is SF5 absolutely stunning to look at. I mentioned the animations already, but the stages look fantastic! The backgrounds are amazing. The characters themselves, WOW, that's all I can say really. I was thinking about going with my "favorites" but really I just like... ALL of them.
Now, there IS one character that I can only wish they'd add to SF5, and that would be Third Strike's 'Q'. His design is so... simple, yet so... great. I mean there's a bunch of characters I'd like them to add other than Q, I'd like to get Sakura and Blanka, and T. Hawk. We all have our character wishes don't we. But the characters that we do have right now are freakin-fan-tastic to look at and play.
* Conclusion *
Yeah long read but anyway... this Street Fighter is just great for me. I love the gameplay, the visuals, the sounds and music and the characters. It's the best fighting game I've played since... hummm... well I haven't played many in the past 10 years to be honest, but I'd say it's the best one since MK9. Actually I prefer SF5 over MK9. I think that I still do prefer the general lore and grittier setting of the Mortal Kombat franchise (especially with MKX, that one as far as visuals go is definitely the best in the MK franchise) but wow has Street Fighter come a LONG way for me since the Arcade and old-school console versions. I might have had even better impressions had I actually bought SF4 because I did like that one. But SF5 is definitely cementing the 'return to form' of this franchise for me. It's very ironic... considering that SF5 is seemingly considered an "average-at-best" fighting game even among the most SF veterans out there; when, for them, this game would be a 5 or 6 out of 10, but for me it's something like a solid 8, maybe even 9.
Just wanted to let all of this off of my shoulders (mostly because of the general "meh" impressions people give of this game... I thought I'd jump in and say how much I actually love this game).

The gameplay? Simple enough. You take two weapons and use them to destroy things. Each weapon usually has a couple different things they can do, but you can use any combination of two, plus a "secret attack," which is a special move that is either related to one of your weapons or a special attack in itself. You also have access to a shield that can block or reflect attacks, and your character isn't half bad at dodge rolling either.
As for the story? Well, I'm sure everyone's heard of the fantastic narrator. You, as the Kid, are tasked with travelling about a world torn asunder by the Calamity and finding Cores to put into a monument in the middle of the Bastion. And for what? Hell, I'm not gonna tell you. Figure it out yourself, but be warned that the story is pretty damn feels inducing. Lots of tear jerkers, sad and glad alike.
Just remember to keep moving forwards. The past is the past, and you should focus on the future. ^^

I went into Neon Drive expecting a somewhat relaxing reflex driver set to some great neo-80s beats.
What I got was a fun but frustrating memory game. Set to some great neo-80s beats.
The core gameplay involves driving your hot 80s sports car down a long straight road and dodging flat panels laying on the ground. This unfortunately brings me to my biggest issue.
The camera focuses directly behind the vehicle, but the obstacles (the flat panels) are laying flat on the ground.
This creates some very serious depth perception issues.
Its incredibly difficult to tell when to switch lanes without touching the panels, especially in sections where you need to have perfect timing to squeeze through small gaps.
I've lost runs several times by lane-switching too early or too late because of how hard it was for me to gauge the distances between my car and the obstacles.
It also doesn't help that there are several dead-end paths with no escape if you go down them- its very difficult to know where these are while trying to pay attention to your own vehicle.
If there were some way to raise the camera up, it'd solve most of the problem here- making it easier to see the obstacles, how big they are and where exactly my car is in the whole mix.
Level 3 is particularly mean. It starts with a long empty road, then after a blinding light it drops you straight into the stage- on the wrong lane.
You can't see the obstacles until the light dissipates, and if you don't change lanes during this part, the lane it defaults you in will result in taking a hit. You have to already know which lane won't hurt you.
Later in the level the camera switches around to a backwards view as you're chased by a spaceship shooting lazers at you.
This was when I realized Neon Drive was a memory game.
The greatest reflexes on the planet wouldn't help you finish this part of the stage, its almost entirely trial and error until you have the lazers memorized so you can pre-emptively prepare your movements.
Thats the only way I was able to beat it.
Despite my gripes, Neon Drive is very fun. It's just also very difficult and frustrating at times.
The price is reasonable and it pays off pretty well if you enjoy these kinds of games.

The Good: Brings back classic 2D fighting, X-Ray moves are brutal and superbly done, all your favorite character are here, Fatalities are unique and brutal, looks and sounds amazing, lots of modes with great online play
The Bad: Still requires memorizing combos, online play requires a strong connection, no characters from MK4 and beyond
"Fatality!", "Finish Him!", "Flawless Victory!", "Get Over Here!". These are just some famous quotes from the infamous Mortal Kombat that everyone knows and remembers. What everyone mainly remembers is the fast paced fighting that has been missed since 1995's Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3. It's been over 15 years since we got a really good and classic feeling MK game, but it's finally here and back with all its bloody gore. Yes the game is still in 3D, but its in what fighting fans like to call "2.5D". The game plays on a 2D playing feel and as soon as you start hammering away on those classic moves and combos you feel the nostalgia seeping into your blood.
The most surprising part about the game isn't the new level of gore, but the amazing story mode. Yes, Mortal Kombat actually has an awesome story mode that plays out far better than last generation's story modes. Instead of some ridiculous adventure mode or scrolling text we get a fully acted, scripted, and voiced story about the actual Mortal Kombat tournament and back story on almost every classic character. The voice acting is actually good and Netherealm Studios actually took the time to bring out each character's personality such as Johnny Cage's smart alack Hollywood attitude. Liu-Kang's eagerness, Kung Lao's jealousy, and Sonya's hotheadedness. The story is done beautifully despite picking up where Armageddon left off. Raiden travels in time to his past self to stop the destruction of armageddon. There are plot twists and even some seriously tense moments in the story that is quite gripping. I can actually say its the best story mode in any fighting game ever made.
However, fans came for the fight and this seriously delivers. Not only are the animations smooth and great to look at, but the controls are as tight as ever. The game responds without any delay and that's what a fighter is all about. Not only is the usual gore back, but the game just packs a serious punch and feels punchy. The hits transfer amazingly well into feelings and that's never been done in an MK game before. The newest things brought to the series are X-Ray moves. Fill you super meter up all the way and you can execute an extremely brutal move that shows your opponent in X-Ray vision and you can see bones crunch, snap, and organs burst. The anatomy is done superbly well with muscles, organs, and everything else in the right place. Each character has their own special skeletal structure so it stays true to the anatomy. I say bravo on Netherealm's part instead of doing it cheaply.
This super meter actually does one other things that I love and these are enhanced moves. Forget the crap from DC Universe completely. When you fill one section of the meter up (it fills up faster when you are getting your butt whooped) you can do the special move while holding down the "Attack Modifier" and it'll change the super move up a little bit and make it more powerful. For example: Doing Jax's Gotcha Grab will only do two hits, but if you enhance it he'll punch them five or six times and do more damage. Do Scorpion's Spear Throw and he'll throw two out for extra damage. These are great and each special attack has its own unique enhancement. This is great for strategists who want to give their fight a little extra kick. The second things you can do with the meter is the usual Breakers, but this requires two pieces to be filled.
For the first time Tag Teaming was put into the game and it works just as great as you'd think. Each character has a special tag out move and it makes the game more intense and just that much more fun. Of course the single player story mode will have you fighting against two people for a challenge, but when you play online or with a friend its an absolute blast. Of course this could have gone all wrong but the team learned from games like Marvel vs Capcom to get it right. This is just one more feature the team got right but could have gone horribly wrong or made the game too unbalanced.
The Fatalities are gory and each character has two plus a Stage Fatality combo. Each character's Fatality can be viewed in the move list in the pause menu, but you have to unlock the second one in the Krypt (more on that later). One thing I have to mention is that Babalities were brought back, but only certain characters can do these. These haven't been since since UMK3! When it comes to fighters there are no characters in here past UMK3. Classics only here and that's for the better. You won't see Kenshi, Kira, Drahmin, Hsu Hao or any of those guys, but there will be DLC add-ins later on so who knows. Each character is beautifully rendered and they fight just like you remember so fans can feel relieved about that. There is one new character and that is Cyber Sub-Zero to tie into the story mode, and he plays differently from the regular Sub-Zero and has some unique moves. Kratos is also an exclusive character for PS3 owners and he plays just like he does in the games complete with some quite time buttons and moves from God of War III. He even has his own unique stage with three different stage fatalities to choose from.
Mortal Kombat has always been known for adding a ton of content in since Deadly Alliance, but this time you're going to like the extras. The Krypt is back with just one type of kurrency this time around and the Krypt has five different sections. Each one has uniquely animated item containers and some are extremely gross, brutal, and gory. I won't spoil it but its very creative. My favorite extra is the Challenge Tower. There are hundreds of challenges that consist of fights that have different parameters such as zombies coming toward you and you have to use Johnny Cage's special Energy Ball move to kill them before they get to you. There's so many I would spend days explaining them but they are great fun and you earn kurrency doing them. One thing I wanted back so bad were the mini-games Test Your Might and Sight last seen in Deadly Alliance. They are back just as great as before, but two new ones were added. Test Your Strike is just like Might but you have to hold the meter inside a box for a few seconds before striking. Test Your Luck has you spinning a wheel and decides the fighter and fighting conditions for you.
Lastly Kombat Kodes were brought back last seen in UMK3, for people who don't know, each character gets three boxes during the loading screen and there are different codes such as headless combat, armless combat, dream combat, upside down combat, X-Rays disabled, blocking disabled, and it just goes on and on. These are used a lot in the challenge tower that I was talking about, but having them in VS is a blast. Lastly the online modes are a must have for any fighter these days and MK was the very first one and seems to be one of the best. While Tag Team and regular 1vs1 are expected a new King of the Hill mode lets you pick an avatar and puts everyone in a room that looks like a theater. The winner keeps fighting everyone in the room until he loses, but people can rate the fight based on a number score and can even cheer or boo the fight. This is a fun mode and is greatly welcomed.
~Score: 9.5/10

Took a break from this game a loooong time ago because it just wasn't my cup of tea, something felt off about it. So here I am three years later, picking it up again... and something still feels off about it.
First, if it wasn't obvious from the bajillion reviews already, this is a sort of action-RPG without much of the RPG part - so basically a top down hack-n-slash. It's 2D in presentation, but everything is very obviously a 3D model.
The environmental art is pretty great, and the music really complements the feel of the world. The main character guy's model looks way beefier than he looks in the promotional artwork for this game, which is a little off putting but completely a matter of opinion.
The thing most people know about this game is the Narrator guy, who both looks and sounds like he should be narrating the adventures of Clint Eastwood in the grittiest cowboy movie ever filmed, but instead somehow found a job narrating the adventures of oddly beefy protag in crumbling world land. I'll give the game credit where it's due here - this isn't something you see almost ever, and it's kind of interesting. You can imagine this story being told around a campfire and sort of have that feeling of visualizing it in your head were you being told it in person, but it has a few hiccups in pretty specific areas where it's just silence for a while until you manage the next thing that triggers the narration. It would be weird if the narrator just never shut up or rambled on, though, so I don't expect him to talk constantly, just... finish the thought in one go. Paying that dude to narrate as much as he did though must have been half the game's budget.
So, gameplay, which is naturally my biggest problem with the game. Your character's kind of slow, and suffers from the same thing Link suffers from - rolling becomes the best option to get anywhere or get anything done. The game would benefit so much from the ability to run and the ability to perform a dash attack, but whatever. Maybe there's a dash attack and I haven't played far enough in to get it, but mechanics that add to the general enjoyment of the game shouldn't be locked behind hours of gameplay. Also I get that there's tons of ranged options, but I just can't abide the enemies floating off the stage somewhere, this is really painful in the timed stages.
Overall I don't think it's the pinnacle of action RPGs, or hack-n-slashes, or really the pinnacle of any game type, unless "campfire story" is a genre, in which case it is a pioneer. It came out of the blue from a development studio that came out of the blue, and when you look at it from that perspective, it's pretty good for that, but that narration budget could have gone a lot farther had it been used in the gameplay department.
Anyway, because "indifference" still isn't an option, I'm going to say no, I don't recommend it. If you want to play a game just to look at pretty scenery, there's better options out there, and the same goes for listening to a good soundtrack or an audiobook - youtube's free. The gameplay has the groundwork of being solid, and isn't buggy nor does it feel rushed, but it desperately needed to be expanded upon.

I bought the game for a 'Predator' experience (IDGAF about the Xenos or Marines) and I wasn't disappointed. AvP 2010 is the definitive 'Predator' game (So far).
The nailed the feeling of playing an omnipotent hunter stalking unwary Marines from above
Thanks to some excellent, innovative mechanics (The assisted jump springs to mind...it should be a standard feature of any Predator game in the future) and level design, hunting humans is extremely satisfying.
What makes it work:
- Using the predator's iconic voice mimicry to distract and lure humans to where you want
- Jumping to great heights and lengths with extreme precision - this makes tree-top navigation fun and fluid
- Target an Alien or a Human for a quick dash strike - this opens them up for a brutal finisher and makes melee feel precise and fluid
- Predator's gadgetry....Chuck a proxy mine, lure in a Marine towards the mine....it never gets old
- Level design that has a lot of verticality and room to move around in
- AI which is *just* dumb enough to keep things fun but smart enough to kill you if you slip up
The options above really let you live out your Predator fantasy. You jump from vantage point to vantage point, lure in your prey, rip skulls and gouge out spines, dash in for a kill and then vanish...reappear again to seperate a spine or two from Marine bodies.
It is gory, brutal and fun.
The Predator levels give you tactical freedom. The mechanics empower you to BE the Predator. This game is to the Predator what the Arkham games are to the Batman - they let you embody the respective characters.
If you like predatory stealth action games like Arkham Asylum/City, Splinter Cell Conviction/Blacklist, Crysis 2/3, Far Cry3/4 where you're stalking unwitting and unwary prey...picking them off one by one....laughing manically as they panic and fret over their rapidly dwindling numbers...then buy Aliens vs Predator 2010.

It's a short 3-4 hour experience and I'm sure you'll have fun with it.
Lost Mission
Nothing too special about this one. Just a 2 Hour long additional level for Doom 3.
Overall, I would highly reccomend Doom 3 BFG Edition.

After a couple of years being a Steam user, I have decided to write my first review as I have noticed this game is highly misunderstood. I have been playing the Street Fighter series since Street Figher II first came out and I remember collecting trollies to get a dollar in return so I could go to the local arcade to play. Living in a very small town, there wasn't many players and I would usually end up playing against the AI through the story mode. I must admit, I wasn't all that good.
Capcom have a noticable pattern with the series bringing out countless iterations of the franchise in what appears to be an attempt to perfect their baby. From amping up the speed, introducing new characters and bringing back some old favourites to adding new super moves or nerfing existing moves, fans of the series should be used to this .
When SFV was announced, I pre-ordered a CE on the PS4 and had high hopes for the game. Like many, I was dissappointed with how Capcom tackled solo play on the game because the only internet connection i had available to me at the time was via a telstra wifi hub which cost about $50 for 3gb of data that would not last long. This was all due to rennovating my home which is now complete and I have since upgraded to an affordable NBN plan. However; I quit SFV because of all the negative reviews it had recieved.
I have been eyeing SFV since and decided to give it another go (a couple of cans of Jack Daniels was also partially responsible). I got the base game on sale from steam and was anxious as I was not looking forward to being disappointed yet again. At first glance, nothing had changed from when i first purchased the game just over a year ago. Being a little under the influence opened my mind a little and i thought to myself, there is no real "Arcade" mode in this game but what does that really mean? What was Capcom thinking? It dawned on me that Capcom have stayed true to the series and are doing what they have been doing in the past with the series and what current are doing today also.
The Street Fighter series has always been known to be a highly competitive game so why would Capcom focus primarily on a so called "arcade" story mode? Well they did in a way because most people don't go to an arcade and play any Street Fighter just to play against an AI. They made it so that the consumer can play in the comfort of their own home against the best rival there can be and that is a human controlled opponent with the story mode taking a back seat. Alot of users are complaining about the price of the DLC content. Well a majority of that content can be unlocked without using your real hard earned $$$. Admittedly I did purchase a couple of alternate costumes as i didn't like the default ones like Ken, Guile and Nashes but they were reasonably priced IMO. People are saying that the game is incomplete because of the Capcom are doing a money grab releasing characters via purchasable DLC. Once again, they can all be unlocked via in-game currency which is not a new concept as many fighting games in the past and present use this method. If you are too lazy to grind and/or get good to be able to unlock what you want, then spend your money but dont be hating on the Developers as without money, they wouldn't be able to bring you these games.
Like it hate it, buy it or not. At the end of the day, what you do with your money is up to you. The devs have produced a game for the fans and Street Fighter is all about Challenging other fighters out there and there's nothing sweeter or more satisfying then beating someone who is higher ranking then you in a nail biting battle. I mean they hold massive Street Fighter competitions for crying out loud. Any way, I think I've babbled on for far too long so here are my pro's and cons:
+Great graphics
+Highly Optimised
+Satisfying competition
+Rewarding
-Price on DLC
-Playing with PS4 opponents (seems to always be laggy)
+/-Learning curve

I bought this game on sale, like a month or two ago, it was on my wishlist for about 3 months then. I downloaded the game and started playing in the same week. So, I'm doing this review about the gameplay:
Once I knew this game I was really hyped at it because I love Point & Click games and it's hard to have really interesting of them here on Steam, so I went straight to see how much it costs, unfortunately, here where I live games are really expensive, so I needed to wait for the sales.
So, I downloaded and started playing the game. It was like one of the most "game beginnings" experiences I've ever had, within all P&C games (even though some adventure games). A deep story, that takes you right to a murder scene, where the survivor is a kid. In the same time I watched that scene, I was shocked. It is not just a "people killed" thing. Both her parents were mutilated on the ground. I even can say I cried at some parts at the end of the game. Play it to know better!
The gameplay is really well done, once you don't get stuck in every corner of the game, you don't need to walk through a whole screen to cross to other places of the game, you can just double-click if you prefer, and it has no bugs at all (at least I didn't find any). You can even interact with a lot of objects in the scenario, and that really made me like it even more.
The game has beautiful and satisfying graphics, kinda Tim Burton themed game. It is, as it seems to be (and about a Easter Egg), all influenced by Alice In Wonderland story, because of the places and characters you see in the game (A Black Cat, some weird bugs and kinda Mad Hatter).
About the soundtrack, it is in short brilliant. Every scene has its own and precise soundtrack, showing how much the developers cared about the details of it.
So, I'd say this game ended as good as I expected, and I don't want any sequel for it.
I loved the job the developers did with the game, and I see how this girl and this dude gave their hearts for it to become perfect.
Graphics: 10/10

I've played all of the Fallout games and I believe Fallout 4 is a good game; I even think it's a good Fallout game, but if I had to pick out the biggest objective flaw with the game it would be that it has a lack of depth.  Had Bethesda doubled down on giving characters, stories, and locations more depth and allowed players to make meaningfully unique choices with lasting consequences we'd see a lot less griping about the game.
In my opinion (maybe ironically), outside of this singular but pervasive issue and the game's technical bugs, a lot of the complaints about FO4 are subjective.  People not liking game features like the settlement system or the voiced protagonist are really matters of personal taste rather than objective problems.  I think most people just wanted more of a true RPG and what they got was an action/sim game with some RPG elements.  It's not necessarily a bad game, just not what people expected, like how Fallout Tactics was more of a real time strategy game than an RPG.﻿
So, I'd say if you're interested, pick it up.

In Northgard,you are playing as one of the few clans and compete with other clans to colonize a new and unknown land. This is done in a RTS gameplay style where you also have to manage and balance your resources. There are multiple win conditions like 'reach X amount of gold,X amount fame,kill the big dragon,forge the legendary sword,research everything' etc. and each clan has different tools to achieve one of those victories.
Map is divided into territories.You start in one,and have to colonize one of the adjacent territories to access it's resources. However your most important resource is your population. Being pioneers of clans,you don't have much people to safely and efficiently spread around,and this also makes yours wars very small scaled.Many players want bigger battles,but I like this better because you have to think before you mindlessly wage war.
There is a winter/summer cycle and of course winters are harsh. You have to get ready for winter during summer.You also have to get ready for random natural disaster type events. Mechanics are quite simple,but there is alot of min-maxing involved,and you have to achieve your goals the fastest way. Even simple things can put a dent in your plans. playing against AI is not much of a challenge,but multiplayer can be quite competitive. Even so,games are quite fast paced and don't take much time like classic RPGs or 4x strategy games which is a great thing for multiplayer gameplay.
Music is relaxing,but definitely need more tracks.Artstyle is colorful and good looking.Interface is simple. I didn't face any bugs,and game ran very smoothly. At this point,any new additions to game will only be plus points. Definitely recommended.

Icey is a really fun side-scrolling action game. The main character, Icey, uses various combos and a quick dash mechanic to fight enemies and bosses. The combat is good, it's fast paced and feels very fair for when you get hit.
The story is basically "go kill enemies", however, what makes it pretty unique is that the game is narrated to you by the developer. The narrator basically tells you to do things and it's up to you if you follow his lead or not. This leads to many funny moments as he gets more annoyed that you're not playing the game properly. This was a really unique aspect and the game would be just fine without it as a great game but I'm so glad it is in there as it adds so much fun dialogue.
It must be noted that Icey is a very short game. I did my first playthrough in just about 3 hours. Then I deleted my save and did a hard mode 100% playthrough. I'm currently at 6.7 hours. So 3.7 hours to do everything (on hard) is quite short.
However, for the price it is, and the enjoyment you get from the narrative and very fun combat mechanics I believe it to definitely be worth it. The soundtrack is really nice too, with a good mix of music.
All in all, it is a fantastic side scrolling hack and slash game with very meta humour. I had a lot of fun with it and definitely would recommend it to anyone.

When you get a game that's that short, it can be awfully difficult to give any kind of attention to it at all.
But Neon Drive, I'm happy to say, defies that, because Neon Drive is the very defenition of quality over quantity.
In making this game, they created something that does exactly what they set out to do, which is admirable, and throughout my (albeit brief) time with the game, I found nothing that looks anything short of spectacular.
The way the backgrounds blend and mesh with the music, the way every single thing is attached to its theme, and yet it doesn't feel compelled to constrain itself by the limitations of the 80s. It creates something special.
I'd be remiss not to reccomend this game, and though some might say 48 minutes is nowhere near $10 worth, why does a pound of food from a three-michelin star restaurant cost $100? It's presentation, gameplay, and quality overcomes its brevity in my eyes, though in the end, I guess it comes down to your budget.

Played this game for many hours. It is very fun, addictive, and enjoyable. But I discovered the further you get, the more Sanctum 2 has a distinct identity crisis. The cohesion of FPS and tower defense breaks down becoming dysfunctional.
This results in the biggest problem Sanctum 2 has: its difficulty curve. The game gets disproportionately more difficult the further you get. Eventually it gets to a point where it becomes impossible to beat levels solo. Eventually it even gets too hard to beat a level in co-op. A lot of this deals with the unreasonable restrictions Sanctum 2 places on players. Some of these are due to Sanctum 2 being designed with a heavy bias towards co-op play. Others are the foolish methods to control which genre the game is trying to be
For example
- There are tons of towers available to unlock, but you're limited to using 4 at a time relying on co-op parters using their 4 tower slots to fill in your deficiencies.
- You're encouraged to corral enemies in an enormous maze BUT
- There's a low restriction on the number of turrets that can be placed.
- Not all turrets are created equally. Some are weak and meant to be replaced by a stronger tower as you unlock them. Unfortunately ranking up is unreasonably slow and requires grinding.
- Not all FPS weapons are created equally. Some characters feature a default weapon (the one you can't change) that is useless weak garbage.
- Certain enemies were designed to bypass turret defenses throwing favor towards FPS elements
- A few of these FPS specific enemies result in a very uneven increase in enemy strength.
- Certain enemies are just plain bawllshiat. Specifically bobblehead enemies that take zero damage from turrets, and can only be damaged and killed by shooting their extremely tiny and constantly moving weak point.
-Some of the later stages you will find yourself losing (typically near the end) because of a wave of these same stupid enemies that take the burden of defeat off your turrets and place it squarely on the player's FPS skills.
The sad thing is I actually like Sanctum 2. It is a good game! I would recommend it if it didn't get so hard for stupid reasons so early in its campaign. That just kills the enjoyment got out of it. If you wish to get Sanctum 2, thankfully it tends to go on sale frequently. The base price for the core game is extremely high and not worth it.

Doom 3 scared the #@$! out of me when I got the XBOX Classic (and later the PC) version - and it's definitely not a worse rendition - the only question is: "is it a good enough rendition all these years on?". "HD" is a terrible word, abused so often. The visuals produced by this game ARE indeed high-resolution (they support 16:9 and 16:10, etc) images, but rather often, a number of textures and most of the geometry isn't quite as "HD" as you'd expect this groundbreaker to be. The game is as moody, claustrophobic, dark and outright terrifying as it ever was, but could truly do much better in the department of visuals - the ground it broke when first released. This is, however, NOT a bad point, more a note of room for improvement.
The audio mostly features surround-sound screams, machine hisses, chants, red herrings and footsteps, while the "music" is still the noise of people suffering over your radio - one of the BEST audio options taken in a game in recent years.
The gameplay is almost identical to the original - little to no health regen (like more games should be IMHO), strafe-and-shoot action, heavy-duty♥♥♥♥♥♥♥extension weaponry and high-res computer screens to interact with. The "duct tape" mod is in action, moving the gameplay to the action end of the spectrum instead of horror (previously, it was light OR gun, making the original game absolutely #$@ing terrifying), but isn't a game-breaker.
People who prefer joypads - I'm one of these as I suffer from rather bad arthiritis in my hands, so save your little opinions and posts flame-warriors - this supports a wired 360 pad very graciously.

The Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing 2 contains all the best elements of the first game, and introduces novelties in form of bigger and more varied skill trees for all three classes and additional mini games, that contribute to the games atmosphere.
In comparison with its predecessor the general level of difficulty has been increased, resulting in a more challenging world of Borgovia, that is filled with original monsters, magic and weird technology. At the same time the skills of your ghostly companion have also been rebalanced, allowing her to support you in your preferred playstyle in a more effective way.
But the greatest strength of Van Helsing lies in its love for detail. Allusions to certain films, comics and the original book by Bram Stoker are proof of that. Furthermore, the protagonist and his delightful ghostly companion will keep you entertained with their wry sense of humor and many snappy dialogues.
Nevertheless, there are a few shortcomings. One of them is the stiff combat system, as already encountered in the first instalment, which would have needed more attention to establish a more fluent hack & slash feeling. Another point is the storyline. While building on the events of the predecessor, the presentation of the story feels rather loveless, making it relatively easy to predict certain story related events.
Please do not open the cell of the familiar looking psychopath with cannibalistic tendencies, who prefers Chianti to certain cuisine. Your fellow resistance fighters will be very grateful for it.

Singleplayer achievements: 59
Multiplayer achievements: 4

Aliens vs Predator 3 is one of my all time favorite games. It is very under-rated. Ill give you a basic run down of the game.
PREDATOR: He is my personal favorite. Movies and games,the predator is like the ultimate hunter. He is very powerful, when taking down marines this can require patience if there are mutiple of them. The predators advantages consist of his health, his weapons, and his claw speed. For his health he has the most health in the game. Him being the biggest one of the three this is not suprising. His weapons are godly poweful. He has four weapons. The campaign starts you with them in this order. Plasma caster, Mines, Smart disc, and Spear.  The plasma caster is a very powerful weapon. If you charge it long enough if it hits it is an automaic one hit. The plasma caster automatically predicts where youre target is going to go and fires there. The proximity mines are essentialey plasma clamores that detect in all directions. This is most effective against marines as they arent fast enough to escape one if they set it off. The smart disc, my favorite weapon, Is a edged disc that is guided by the laser on your mask when you throw it. It can bounce off of walls an absured amount of times and make the enemy♥♥♥♥♥♥their pants. If it hits the body it leaves any species with one light melee attack left in them. On hitting the head the target will instantly die. This works against predators often as their head is pretty big. Now finally for the spear. I feel like this one would have made first if it werent for my love of the disc. The spear is a skillshot weapon that can miss often. If it does hit it is a guaranteed kill. That is it for the predator other than the fact that it is harder to knock him down and while his light atack is slower than the aliens his heavy attack is much faster.

ALIEN: The alien is a more aggressive charcter in general. The alien has only its melee, to make up for this it has the most mobility in the entire game. It can climb on any surface. Its heavy attack is an insant if they are on the wall. It wont do full heavy attack damage if you dont hit them in the head. If you do manage to hit them in the head they are pretty much screwed. As it stuns and does alot of damage. A second tail will usually kill them. The alien can be very prone to dieing if they fight up too close to their target and make their approach obvious. The alien has the second most health in the game. In melee combat what they have superior to the predator is their light attack is much faster. Their heavy attack although slower stuns longer. Their finishing moves AKA grabs are usually faster. This can be an upside or a down-side depending on how you look at it, but the alien automatically regenerates health.
MARINE: The marine is sterotyped as the worst character in the game. He is not. The reason his seems to be is he is very difficult although when mastered is a hell hole to deal with. The marine has the lowest health and mobility. The marine fights with guns.
GUNS:
Pistol: It is his weakest weapon although it has unlimited ammo.
Pulse rifle: It is his auto-matic assult rifle. It is the all around weapon. It has alot of ammo its mag size being 99. Jesus. PS You also get to start with this is multiplayer when you spawn. Its secondary fire is a grenade. AKA Noob toob for cod players.
Shotgun: If you have enemies that like to pounce at you instead of blocking try to hit them with this last second. The shotgun is a very up-close weapon its secondary fire is a buckshot that will stun and instakill if close enough.
Sniper: My favorite weapon. If you hit all shots in the body it will three hit. Don't let that fool you into thinking its bad. Its semi automatic so this seems op to some players. The second shot will stun too. If you hit an alien or predator in the head they will be stunned so finish them with one more bullet as headshots will leave them with low enough health to die to this.
Smartgun: The marines last but not least weapon. This is like a minigun except with a square on your screen that it has aimbot in. This thing is the bain of predator players. It will detect them while they are invisible. The only downsides to this weapon are having low ammo. Cant run while holding it and it takes up two weapon slots.

The general curse of an FPS game is lack of plot and Sanctum is very scarcely different. It will relay a comic book-style preamble before every encounter but you will mostly find yourself more worried about the map layout of the upcoming battle than the story itself and in the end I think most peopel aren't going to know the story behind the Core Guardians at all. Though those of you who do, aren't going to think it's anything to write home about - I didn't anyway.
Assuming you're using mouse and keyboard (because why would you use a game pad for a FPS...?) the control setup is what you might call standard, but it's called standard for a reason - it works. The pace of each map is always scaled perfectly in my opinion and each time you start a new encounter the difficulty scales well, whether you're playing with friends or on your own. I will say Sanctum will test you - even if you're the type to hunt up tower placement strategies with a little Google Fu you're still going to have to be up to snuff with your shooter skills - Sanctum 2 will send enemies that will reflect fire, take several minutes to take down, and can even destroy your towers from multiple directions. And while it's easy to predict what comes from where and what you should have readied in defense, a lot of the time the enemy AI isn't static. Which is a good thing. No stale battles here!
While the menu music is a bit of a snooze the in game battle tunes really set a mood well - prog electro and D&B compliment Sanctum's futuristic theme perfectly. There are times with REX you will have to endure a plethora of stacked explosion sounds however as well as some of the tower and enemy sound effects.
The biggest gripe I have with how the game looks is in a few of the stages the lighting will be so intense it will seem like you're trying to engage in a staring contest with a star from 5 feet away through a magnifying glass though the environments, character and monster designs and weaponry of the game are beautiful. The menus and maps are nicely done as per the theme of the game though foregoing things like grass and physical damage for textures is a bit of a letdown, it's not too terribly noticable.
Sanctum is a very unique blend of first person shooter and tower defense, and the first of it's kind even. There are even some bits and bobs of RPG thrown in there with the games leveling system, though they work really well. If you've played the original you'll note how much has improved in the series thus far and that gets a major amount of respect from me (mainly because I made the mistake of playing the second installment first and had to backpedal into something I felt really couldn't match up.) The highly customizable pre-battle outfittings and DLC maps and overall difficulty of the game (which can be augmented with Feats of Strength, which are kind of like handicaps and modifiers to make the difficulty even more trying) make it one I can constantly play over and over again. I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a different kind of shooter.

The sheer amount of content makes this game worth the price tag, but if you get it on sale like I did, you are in for a massive treat. Doom 3: BFG Edition is a bundle of the original three DOOM games (plus all of the expansions ever released) which have been remastered and re-released with steamworks integration for modern operating systems.
On a personal note, the first three DOOM games are some of the best games I've ever played and historically are some of the most revolutionary games ever released. This is due to the fact that these games are designed to be fun - it's quite obvious that the story plays second fiddle to the gameplay. The level design is some of the best I've played, and the graphics were revolutionary for the time (although they don't really hold up by today's standards).
Despite my gushing, there are some flaws - not with the original standalone games, but with the way that they have been remastered. The biggest complaint is about Doom 3's lighting and flashlight mechanics. A fundamental feature of Doom 3 was that it was a really dark game, where sometimes it was impossible to see if there were enemies in front of you, which added to it's claustrophobic nature. In order to see you had to manually switch to your flashlight and quickly switch back to your weapon in order to shoot something. However, in the BFG Edition, everything is lit up a bit more, and the flashlight (which is rarely used) is now "shoulder-mounted" - so you can use it and shoot at the same time, which makes the game a whole lot more easy. This also means that the outdated textures aren't hidden in the shadows, and if you're a graphics orientated person, this can start to annoy you.
There are also some some technical faults. The main one is that you can't ALT-TAB without going out of fullscreen mode first. The console has been locked and the only way to unlock it is with commands in the game launch options. And finally, whenever I take a screenshot with F12, the game disables achievements, because for some reason it thinks I am opening the console, which is extremely annoying, because the console is locked!
Despite it flaws, I would highly recommend this game, it has been one of my most enjoyable gaming experiences this year thus far (despite coming out almost four years ago). This is a great way to experience the DOOM franchise while waiting for the new DOOM game to become a bit cheaper.

So Doom 3: BFG Edition gets some real stick from critics and fans alike. The main criticisms are drawn from the controls, specifically the missing out of a hotkey weapon system, which is definitely, given the fast paced nature of the game and the variety of enemies, a big minus. Sometimes you want to rocket launcher those Cacodemons, Plasma Gun these Hell-knights and then finish off with a good old fashioned punch-up with those zombies and you want to be able to do that in the same area instead of having to decide who's getting fisted and where. It's a lot like real life in that respect.
The other problem is the use of the flashlight in the game. In the original Doom 3, whenever there's a darkened area the player has to whip out the flashlight to see and can't use a weapon unless they actively switch to one, and then there's no flashlight. This sounds like an improvement but it's actually not. It was very tense exploring those dark corners practically unarmed and then if♥♥♥♥♥♥went down you had no choice but to whip out the ol' chainsaw and wildly slash at the shadows. It's these two big decisions that add an element of hand-holding which has NEVER been what Doom is about.
Fans have also complained, and rightly so, that the Doom and Doom II games included in the package are CENSORED, some Nazi memorabilia and placement of crosses and things were taken out. This has never occured in Doom history either and consdering the fame and legendary status the series garnered from being controversial 20 years ago, it's a totally unneccessary diservice to the fans.
That aside, Doom 3 and it's expansion Resurrection of Evil, are largely untouched weirdly (one would assume that the more recent game would be the likely candidate for censorship but no). They are the same save for marginally improved visuals, a bit more gore and an auto-save system which also got some negative press but I rather like.
The reason I play Doom is sometimes when you come home from work, you don't want to be dazzled by story or made to think and reflect. You want to be brow-beaten by legions of demons, splattered with blood and deafened by explosions and taken to your happy-place. It may say something odd about me that my happy-place is Hell but I know I'm not alone in feeling this, everyone loves Doom.
This version, as I stated, contains (censorship aside) the full versions of Doom, Doom II and Doom 3, all expansions and a short new single-player campaign. ID have dumped on us, to make up for shortcomings, an absolute truckload of Doom to consume. This is fine by me, and when I play it I have a blast. So if you don't care that much about the aforementioned controversies and just want Doom, go for it, it's convenient and it's all in one place. However, if you care about the evils of censorship and don't want to be seen to support it, just buy them individually, it's not much of a trade-off. I wish I did that.
Still gets a thumbs up from me anyway.

Damn near one of the best RTS out there, probably one of the ebst early access games i have ever seen or played. This game is pretty much all PROS, althought there are definately somethings that can be tweaked and or adjusted.
Pros: A true base builder, meaning your not going to spam 10000's of buildings into a single area, you need to gear up some warriors and take territories to expand. Citizens like upgrades, meaning building 100 of♥♥♥♥♥♥houses wont make them happy, if your clan is thriving they like to feel the part. Resources seem actually earned next to just some gold mine where your tractors go and come back. Dividing up citizens at different times early to get wood, or to farm food can make a difference later on with trading.
Map cycle keeps the game fun and exciting, from stocking up in summer, then hunkering down in winter to survive the snow, especially when a blizzard is on your doorstep. The games event cycle, although only like four events, keeps it a true strategy, You certainly have to plan when to attack and when to defend, cgetting caught losing your troops in winter means the other clans can quickly overcome you.
While there are many many other pros, my cons list (at least for now in the early acccess includes.
Clans right now dont seem balanced, none of them are like♥♥♥♥♥♥but there are defiantely some better than others. Fenris attack damage can let you take the map rather quickly, and owning warriors brings happiness. WHile a good feature i found myself just growing food, houses, and warrior camps then setting out to conquer my opponets. The ship raiding clan ((their name escapes my mind at the moment)) is incredibly powerful as well. Some others are focused around  reasource wins, or lore wins.. which half the time ive never even reached unless in a solo game.
if your wondering if you should buy this, and your an RTS fan.. save yourself the pain and do. Definately everything the  reviews make it to be. Im more of a large scale 10000+ troop warfare, but this game is just so well made it makes up for it all!

It's hard to reccomend a game with so little to it. At this point, I've beaten every level the game has to offer, and more, (having beaten a few hard modes and on the road to one insane mode,(pun not intended, unfourtonatly because it was great)), but it's only taken, at the time of review, 48 minutes.
When you get a game that's that short, it can be awfully difficult to give any kind of attention to it at all.
But Neon Drive, I'm happy to say, defies that, because Neon Drive is the very defenition of quality over quantity.
In making this game, they created something that does exactly what they set out to do, which is admirable, and throughout my (albeit brief) time with the game, I found nothing that looks anything short of spectacular.
The way the backgrounds blend and mesh with the music, the way every single thing is attached to its theme, and yet it doesn't feel compelled to constrain itself by the limitations of the 80s. It creates something special.
I'd be remiss not to reccomend this game, and though some might say 48 minutes is nowhere near $10 worth, why does a pound of food from a three-michelin star restaurant cost $100? It's presentation, gameplay, and quality overcomes its brevity in my eyes, though in the end, I guess it comes down to your budget.

What to say that hasn't already been said? I'm certainly not chiming in to repeat its glory but rather because where else can I cement my feelings about the game. It was surprising in its emotional depth. I literally laughed and cried, and its soundtrack has gotten so much airplay outside of the game with me that it's now ground into my bones.
Going in, having gotten it as part of a bundle, I expected little. The chitzy narration I thought would grow obnoxious, instead it became endearing, and as layers of the narrators character and perspective are slowly revealed.. a clever twist on expectations. Like finding out the sins of trusted relatives.
There are multiple endings, but the one I chose made my heart soar, and was the subject of conversation between my friends and I for days afterward. This game proved to me that simple elegant design could triumph over technical highs for games, and I've been exploring platformers and beat-em-ups on steam ever since.
